before.title: Projects: create a new project and move builds between projects; move every pending build older than 2 days into a new project
before.detail: 1) Add create-project (valid project manifest, its own builds, notes, data; per the multi-project setup where picking a project switches all data) and move-builds-between-projects, by UI and full API (no AI). 2) Then create a new project and move every Pending build created before 2026-11-08 out of the current project into it, with their notes, steps, branches and history intact; nothing deleted or archived. Builds from the last two days stay. Report the list moved.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Queued by console.
Split by Claude into 10 steps (1 Fable).

origin.said: I don't want to archive. I want to move to another, you know how we set it up from multiple projects. Each one has its own builds, its own notes, all that. Make a new project, remove those from this project and move them to the new project.

steps.text: Design the project contract. Write the project manifest schema covering id, name, created, and the builds, notes and data roots. Define move-build semantics: a build's store entry, journal lines, notes, steps, branches, PR links, reports, shipped records and change entries all move together and keep their ids. Specify the order of operations so a move is atomic (write the target with tmp files, then remove from the source, roll back on failure) and how id collisions are handled. Confirm that a project switch already switches all build data, and write the contract to a doc.
steps.why: Cross-project data contract and schema design that every later step and app depends on

steps.text: Build the createProject core library. Validate the manifest against the schema, scaffold the project's own builds, notes and data folders, register it in the projects registry and the /projects hub sync, and refuse duplicate ids. It is a pure function with no AI. Add unit tests.

Build the moveBuilds core library, following the contract from step 1. Move the selected builds between projects: store entries, journal entries, notes, steps, reports, shipped records and change-entry refs. Git branches and PRs are left untouched, but their references are kept. Writes are atomic with rollback, and a dry-run returns the planned list. Nothing is deleted or archived; the source only loses the moved entries. Add unit tests, including a failure halfway through a move.

Add REST routes for the console API. POST /api/projects creates a project. GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/:id read state. POST /api/projects/:id/move-builds takes {buildIds|filter:{state,createdBefore}, dryRun} and moves builds. GET /api/projects/:id/builds lists a project's builds. Add route tests.

Expose the same actions through the other three channels, all calling the same library functions with the same arguments. MCP: console actions project.create, project.list, project.get and project.moveBuilds. CLI: axf project create|list|show|move-builds with --dry-run, --state and --created-before. Voice: AmberX intents for 'create project X' and 'move builds to project X'.

Add the UI. A New project dialog in the project picker. In the Build manager, multi-select with a 'Move to project…' action that shows a dry-run preview and asks for confirmation. Add the deep links console_show/console_open targets projects/new, projects/<id> and builds/move?ids=…, register them, and make dialog state readable through the API from step 4.

Run end-to-end tests of create and move on a scratch fixture through REST, MCP and CLI. Check that the results match across channels, that history and notes are intact after a move, that switching to the target project shows the moved builds, and that the source no longer lists them.

Do a dry run against the real data. Using the API, list every build in the current project (amberx-axf) whose state is Pending and that was created before 2026-11-08T00:00. Save the list with ids, titles, created dates and branches. Confirm that builds from 2026-11-08 onward are excluded.

Do the real move. Create the new project through the API (id amberx-axf-backlog unless one is already defined, and record the chosen name). Move the dry-run list into it. Verify the counts before and after, check that every moved build's notes, steps, journal and branch refs are present in the target, and confirm nothing was deleted or archived. Commit the data changes.

Finish the build. Run the full test suite. Write the report to _claude/builds/reports/projects-create-a-new-project-and-move-builds-be.md, including the moved-builds list and how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, with the API access paths listed in its description.

# Build: orchestrator-assigns-builds-steps-to-employee-ag

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T16:28:04.849Z
> When the orchestrator assigns builds or steps they are sent to the right employee who has its own set of briefs to send back to the orchestrator and uses the employee data in the brief. In the group chat the orchestrator asks if anyone can do something, if they have skills or tools or capabilities; the first one to take it opens a dialog listing all the matching agents with a percentage of each one being the best choice for the job. After the 90 second veto it chooses the best probable one by default.

In the group chat the orchestrator asks if anyone can do something, if they have skills or tools or capabilities; the first one to take it opens a dialog listing all the matching agents with a percentage of each one being the best choice for the job. After the 90 second veto it chooses the best probable one by default."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step orchestrator-assigns-builds-steps-to-employee-ag <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). steps.text: Design the inventory contract: a versioned JSON schema for one plugin's UI inventory (elements with kind dialog/table/button/pane/window/tab/other, parent/child ids, behaviors as event→action entries, layout/style/colour tokens with source and resolved value, groups and roots), plus the skin contract (a per-plugin skin manifest of token overrides, layout overrides and behavior toggles, keyed by plugin id and versioned so revert is exact). steps.why: Cross-port contract every plugin's UI must satisfy, used by inventory, views and skins

steps.text: Framework skin scoping: add a plugin-scoped skin layer to the framework so a skin applies only inside one plugin's mount root (scoped CSS custom properties and layout overrides under the plugin's container, behavior toggles through the existing component props), with load order room theme → plugin skin and a no-op when no skin is set. Same component code underneath.
steps.why: Changes how GUIs render across all apps: a new framework layer between room theme and plugin

steps.text: Framework inventory hooks: expose a read-only introspection walk over a mounted plugin (component tree, registered dialogs/windows/tabs, bound event handlers, resolved tokens) that returns data matching the inventory schema, without changing plugin code.

Viewer shell with IDE-style tab groups (split, drag tabs between groups, each tab is one view on one root) and the root/group picker: choose any element as root, define and save named groups of elements.
Grid view with expandable rows (element, kind, behaviors, tokens; filter, sort, search) and classic tree view, both rooted at the selected root or group.
3D view: elements as nested layered boxes by containment depth, orbit/zoom, click to select and sync selection with the other views; falls back to tree when WebGL is missing.

API for the viewer: deep links for plugin, view, root, group and tab layout; state read (open tabs, views, root, selection, groups); actions open_view, set_root, select, create/rename/delete group, move tab, export inventory (JSON/CSV). REST + MCP + CLI + voice, all four the same.

AI reskin behind the plugin's AI switch: when on, send the inventory and goal to the configured model to propose a skin; output goes through the same validator; when off, the option is hidden and the API returns a clear 'AI is off' error.
Reskin UI: 'Rebuild this plugin' panel with goal picker, override editor, side-by-side live preview (skin applied only inside a preview mount of the plugin), Apply, one-click Revert and skin history.

API for reskin: deep link to the reskin panel for a plugin; state read (active skin, preview skin, history); actions generate, preview, apply, revert, revert_to <version>, set override, AI switch setting. REST + MCP + CLI + voice, all four the same.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Screenshots and everything of what it did? Yep.

steps.text: Define the contract between Shipped Features entries and the shared screenshot registry: how a build id/name maps to its screenshots, how before/after pairs are marked (role: before|after|shot, pair key, caption, captured_at, source = registry|ui-review), and the fallback lookup through UI Review screenshots grouped by build name. Write it as a schema doc and a JSON schema both sides read; if the shared screenshot registry build has not landed, define the read interface it must satisfy.
steps.why: Cross-port contract between the screenshot registry, UI Review and Shipped Features

steps.text: Server side: add a resolver that, for a shipped build, collects its screenshots from the shared screenshot registry (and UI Review screenshots grouped by build name as fallback), pairs before/after shots, dedupes, and returns them sorted and capped per the contract. Cache per build id.

REST API: GET /api/shipped/:id/screenshots (list, pairs, counts) and GET /api/shipped/:id/screenshots/:shot (one shot with metadata and image URL); include screenshot count and cover thumbnail on the existing shipped list/entry responses. Settings for the gallery (default view grid|before-after, thumbnail size, show on list on/off) readable and writable at GET/PUT /api/shipped/settings/gallery.

UI: on each Shipped Features entry show an inline screenshot strip (cover + count) and a gallery view: grid of shots, before/after side-by-side or slider for pairs, lightbox with prev/next and captions, empty state when the build has none. Built on the console plugin framework components.

API parity for the gallery UI: deep links console_show/console_open targets shipped-features/<build id>/screenshots and shipped-features/<build id>/screenshots/<shot> (opens gallery or lightbox at that shot, before/after mode); gallery state readable (open build, current shot, view mode); actions open_gallery, show_shot, next/prev, set_view, and gallery settings registered as console actions for MCP.

CLI and voice: add 'shipped screenshots <build> [--shot n] [--before-after] [--open]' and 'shipped gallery settings get|set' plugin commands calling the same REST/actions; add AmberX voice intents ('show me the screenshots for <build>', 'next shot', 'before and after') mapped to the same actions.

Tests: resolver (registry hit, UI Review fallback, before/after pairing, no screenshots), REST endpoints and settings, deep link parsing, action/MCP/CLI/voice parity (same results through all four), and a UI test that the gallery renders and the lightbox navigates. Then write the report _claude/builds/reports/shipped-features-show-each-landed-build-s-screen.md (what changed, screenshots of the gallery, how each UI part is reached via deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice), add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating the API reach for every UI piece and the dependency on the shared screenshot registry build.

before.title: Dispatcher: a worktree store write can erase a fresh launch record (double launch, then a stuck build)
before.detail: Seen on pass-approval-hook-deep-link-amberx-notification, Nov 10 2026 (journal _claude/builds/journal/2026-11-p4.jsonl): 18:11:16 pipeline:launch wrote status running + pipeline.session earl; 18:11:19 the worktree's orchestrator:note ('Claude account: ...', written by claude-headless.sh at start from a store copy taken before the launch) landed with status queued and no pipeline record, and the per-build newer-wins merge kept it; 18:12:11 the next tick launched the same build again (gina), both runs numbered 1. Earl's 's1 done' tick at 18:24:48 erased the second record the same way, so the live build sat in 'running' with no session: checkEnds and reapBuilds both skip a build without pipeline.session / pipeline.account, so the phase end was never handled (set to queued by hand). Fix, in this order: (1) builds-merge-core: merge the pipeline record per field, never let an incoming copy with no pipeline record replace a newer launch record on main (or have orchestrator.mjs act pull main's record before a note/tick write); (2) pipeline-core plan(): never launch a build whose status is running/waiting or that has a running or queued agent slot for its id (agent-slots status lists build per slot); (3) checkEnds/reapBuilds: a build 'running' with no pipeline record and no live slot for it ends by the phase rule (exit 0 + model switch -> queued) instead of being skipped forever; (4) claude-headless.sh: write the 'Claude account' note only after the launch record is published, or through the per-field merge. Add a check in framework/spec/check-builds-live.mjs that replays this journal sequence.

before.title: Molly gap: axHub allows Molly's origin on /auth/api/* (CORS with credentials) so native screens read the hub session
before.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. From https://molly.amberxai.com, GET https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/api/session answers 200 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and the preflight OPTIONS /auth/api/logout answers 200 with no CORS headers, so a browser on Molly cannot read the hub session or post a write. The hub should answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins (Molly first) on /auth/api/* with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true, Access-Control-Allow-Headers content-type, accept, x-axhub-csrf, Vary Origin; never * with credentials. The session cookie is same-site (SameSite=Lax is enough). Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (axhub provider, credentials include, X-AxHub-CSRF on writes).

before.title: Molly gap: Expenses allows Molly's origin on /api/expenses/v1/* (CORS with credentials) so native screens read the ledger
before.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. From https://molly.amberxai.com, GET https://expenses.amberxai.com/api/expenses/v1/entries?limit=1 answers 401 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin and the preflight answers 204 with no CORS headers, so a browser on Molly cannot call the ledger API with the axs_session cookie. The route handler (apps/expenses/app/api/expenses/v1/[...path]/route.ts, or proxy.ts) should answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin, Allow-Credentials true, Allow-Headers content-type, accept, authorization, x-expenses-user, Allow-Methods GET POST PATCH OPTIONS, Vary Origin, and an OPTIONS handler. What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 19:21):

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

before.title: Every UI element is a named asset
before.detail:
Apply the rule across schemas/asset-types.json, the web and Android ports, the 39 starter assets and the conformance fixtures.

- Two tiers: element assets (button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label...) and parent assets (toolbar, menu, nav, app menu, dialog, container, window). A standalone element in a layout is its own named asset; groups only exist inside a parent asset.
- Namespaced ids for every asset (e.g. axf.button.save, axf.toolbar.editor); layouts and parents reference ids.
- Split instance (label, icon, action, state) from skin (style asset + theme tokens).
- Slots with type contracts in layout regions and parents; hot-swap and drag-and-drop = rebinding a slot to a compatible asset id.
- Kernel unchanged (open type registry).

Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Design note first: write `_claude/memory/docs/named-assets.md` — the two tiers (element assets: button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label; parent assets: toolbar, menu, nav, app-menu, dialog, container, window), the id namespace rule (`<ns>.<type>.<name>`, e.g. `axf.button.save`), instance vs skin split, and which existing starter ids change. List every file the rule touches. No code.

BRETT: review the design note. Decide (a) whether existing starter ids are renamed in place or aliased (old id keeps resolving), (b) whether element assets are required for every control or opt-in per app. Record both answers in the note and in `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Schema: in `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` add `"tier": "element" | "parent"` to every type and a top-level `idRule` (regex, documented) for namespaced ids; keep `optional: true` on new fields so old apps validate. Run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` and `axf validate --framework` — both must pass unchanged.

Validator (web): `framework/core/validate.ts` → `validateAsset` warns (not errors, until the switch flips) when an id does not match `idRule`; add `assetTier(type)`. Add 4 cases to `framework/spec/fixtures/validation.json` (good namespaced id, bare id, element, parent). `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts` then CI check.

Validator (Kotlin + CLI): mirror the id rule in `framework/android/axf-kernel/.../asset/` validator and in the build-engine validator (`framework/cli/build-engine.mjs` validateAsset). Same fixture cases replayed by `ConformanceTest` (written without a compiler: check the "CI build errors" issue after push).

Element asset types, part 1: add `toggle`, `input`, `icon` as `tier: element` types in `asset-types.json` (data shape: label, icon, action, state keys; skin = style-theme tokens only). One starter each under `framework/assets/<type>/`. `axf validate --framework` passes.

Element asset types, part 2: mark the existing `button`, `slider`, `label` as `tier: element`; add the instance/skin split to their spec (`data.instance` {label, icon, action, state} vs `data.skin` {style tokens}) with the old flat shape still accepted by `asEnvelope` normalisation. Fixture cases in `components.json`.

Parent slots: in `asset-types.json` give every parent type (toolbar, app-menu, nav-menu, context-menu, dialog, container, window) a `slots` block like `layout.slots` (named slots + accepted element types), reusing `compileSlots`/`regionAccepts` from `framework/core/engines/layout.ts`. Fixture cases in `layout-slots.json` for one parent.

Rebinding = hot-swap: `framework/core/runtime.ts` gets `bindSlot(parentType, parentId, slot, elementId)` / `unbindSlot` (stored like `attachToHost` in `widgets.ts`, settings key `axf.bind.<parent>.<slot>`); `swap()` of a parent keeps bindings whose types still fit. Unit cases in `widgets.json` → `bindings`.

Kotlin runtime parity: `AxfRuntime.bindSlot/unbindSlot` + KV `<key>:bind` in the kernel, same rules as the TS version, replaying the `bindings` fixture in `ConformanceTest`. Written without a compiler; push and read the CI issue.

Rename the 39 starter assets to namespaced ids (`axf.<type>.<name>`) with the alias map chosen in step 2 (`framework/assets/aliases.json`, read by `registry.ts` + Kotlin `AssetRegistry`): every app manifest and `framework/defaults.json` still resolve. `axf validate --framework` + `validate apps/demo` + console `npm run build` pass.

React layer: `framework/react/components/Controls.tsx` renders an element asset by id (`<AssetButton id>` etc.) reading instance + skin; a standalone element in a layout region renders through the same path. Element Explorer (`react/studio/Inspector.tsx`) shows tier + bindings.

Compose layer: `axf-ui/components/Buttons.kt`, `Slider.kt`, `Controls.kt` take an element asset id the same way; `ElementExplorer.kt` shows tier + bindings. Android console showcase renders one bound element in its toolbar.

Flip the switch: `idRule` violations become errors for apps with `frameworkVersion` ≥ the new one (old apps keep warnings), `axf init` writes namespaced ids, templates updated. Run the CI template sweep locally (`axf init` for react-ts, next-ts, android-compose + validate).

Docs + close: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Named assets"; CLAUDE.md Status bullet; decisions.md entry; mark the pending item complete and the plan feature built; differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/named-asset-rule.md` (rule for rebuilds).

steps.text: Design note first: write `_claude/memory/docs/named-assets.md` — the two tiers (element assets: button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label; parent assets: toolbar, menu, nav, app-menu, dialog, container, window), the id namespace rule (`<ns>.<type>.<name>`, e.g. `axf.button.save`), instance vs skin split, and which existing starter ids change. List every file the rule touches. No code.

BRETT: review the design note. Decide (a) whether existing starter ids are renamed in place or aliased (old id keeps resolving), (b) whether element assets are required for every control or opt-in per app. Record both answers in the note and in `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Schema: in `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` add `"tier": "element" | "parent"` to every type and a top-level `idRule` (regex, documented) for namespaced ids; keep `optional: true` on new fields so old apps validate. Run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` and `axf validate --framework` — both must pass unchanged.

Validator (web): `framework/core/validate.ts` → `validateAsset` warns (not errors, until the switch flips) when an id does not match `idRule`; add `assetTier(type)`. Add 4 cases to `framework/spec/fixtures/validation.json` (good namespaced id, bare id, element, parent). `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts` then CI check.

Validator (Kotlin + CLI): mirror the id rule in `framework/android/axf-kernel/.../asset/` validator and in the build-engine validator (`framework/cli/build-engine.mjs` validateAsset). Same fixture cases replayed by `ConformanceTest` (written without a compiler: check the "CI build errors" issue after push).

Element asset types, part 1: add `toggle`, `input`, `icon` as `tier: element` types in `asset-types.json` (data shape: label, icon, action, state keys; skin = style-theme tokens only). One starter each under `framework/assets/<type>/`. `axf validate --framework` passes.

Element asset types, part 2: mark the existing `button`, `slider`, `label` as `tier: element`; add the instance/skin split to their spec (`data.instance` {label, icon, action, state} vs `data.skin` {style tokens}) with the old flat shape still accepted by `asEnvelope` normalisation. Fixture cases in `components.json`.

Parent slots: in `asset-types.json` give every parent type (toolbar, app-menu, nav-menu, context-menu, dialog, container, window) a `slots` block like `layout.slots` (named slots + accepted element types), reusing `compileSlots`/`regionAccepts` from `framework/core/engines/layout.ts`. Fixture cases in `layout-slots.json` for one parent.

Rebinding = hot-swap: `framework/core/runtime.ts` gets `bindSlot(parentType, parentId, slot, elementId)` / `unbindSlot` (stored like `attachToHost` in `widgets.ts`, settings key `axf.bind.<parent>.<slot>`); `swap()` of a parent keeps bindings whose types still fit. Unit cases in `widgets.json` → `bindings`.

Kotlin runtime parity: `AxfRuntime.bindSlot/unbindSlot` + KV `<key>:bind` in the kernel, same rules as the TS version, replaying the `bindings` fixture in `ConformanceTest`. Written without a compiler; push and read the CI issue.

Rename the 39 starter assets to namespaced ids (`axf.<type>.<name>`) with the alias map chosen in step 2 (`framework/assets/aliases.json`, read by `registry.ts` + Kotlin `AssetRegistry`): every app manifest and `framework/defaults.json` still resolve. `axf validate --framework` + `validate apps/demo` + console `npm run build` pass.

React layer: `framework/react/components/Controls.tsx` renders an element asset by id (`<AssetButton id>` etc.) reading instance + skin; a standalone element in a layout region renders through the same path. Element Explorer (`react/studio/Inspector.tsx`) shows tier + bindings.

Compose layer: `axf-ui/components/Buttons.kt`, `Slider.kt`, `Controls.kt` take an element asset id the same way; `ElementExplorer.kt` shows tier + bindings. Android console showcase renders one bound element in its toolbar.

Flip the switch: `idRule` violations become errors for apps with `frameworkVersion` ≥ the new one (old apps keep warnings), `axf init` writes namespaced ids, templates updated. Run the CI template sweep locally (`axf init` for react-ts, next-ts, android-compose + validate).

Docs + close: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Named assets"; CLAUDE.md Status bullet; decisions.md entry; mark the pending item complete and the plan feature built; differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/named-asset-rule.md` (rule for rebuilds).

before.title: Asset Browser plugin
before.detail: Browse, preview, import, export and hot-swap assets across apps built on AXF. Installed by default.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Plugin skeleton `apps/console-web/plugins/asset-browser` from `_template` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-browser`, lifecycle, install/uninstall, nav → Plugins → Asset browser, settings sub-tab). Lifecycle check + console build pass.

Sources: server route `GET /api/plugins/asset-browser/sources` lists asset folders it may read: framework starters (`framework/assets`), every app under `apps/*/src/assets` or `app/src/main/assets/axf` (from `framework/cli/app-bundle.mjs list`), designed assets (asset-designer dataDir when present). Never follows symlinks; roots only.
Browse view: grid by type → source → asset, search box (reuses `consoleSearch.ts` provider pattern), type chips from `asset-types.json`, counts per source. Rows show id, label, origin, tier.

Preview: `AssetPreview.tsx` from `framework/react/studio` renders the selected asset in a card; for chrome types a live preview on an `ab-preview-<type>` swap like theme-manager; "Apply here" = `rt.swap(type, id)` after `registry.register`.

Import: drop/paste JSON or pick a file → `validateAsset` → preview → install into a chosen target (console runtime, or an app folder through `POST /api/plugins/asset-browser/install {source, target, type, id}` that writes the file only inside allowed app asset folders; built-in ids refused; backups under the plugin dataDir).

Export: single asset or a pack (zip of asset@1 files + `pack.json`), served by `GET …/export?ids=`; packs are what the plugin runtime (`x.plugins`, PACK kind) will load later, so write the `pack@1` shape now in `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json`.

Hot-swap across apps: for apps running `axf dev` (`framework/cli/dev-server.mjs`), "Push to device" posts the asset to the dev server's folder so the HotReloader picks it up; list dev servers from settings (`axf.devServer`). Error card when none.

Installed by default + Android: enabled in console plugin defaults, `plugins.json` catalog entry, `plugins.mjs --check`; Android `axf-devtools` route `asset-browser` showing the bundled assets by type with Apply (uses `AssetRegistry` + `AxfRuntime.swap`), so Settings → Plugins lists it on both ports.
Tests: `test.py` (sources never leave roots, import validation, built-in refusal, export pack shape), lifecycle check, CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-browser.md` + LOG.md + web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.browser` built, pending complete.

before.title: Asset templates: 10+ per type + defaults
before.detail: At least 10 editable templates/boilerplates for every asset type the designer covers, plus a default asset per type.

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.
Nov 3 2026: Build Pilot is retired; s13 only covers the console's asset designer now.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Template index: `framework/assets/templates/index.json` (`asset-templates@1`: id, type, label, tags, file) + loader `listAssetTemplates(type)` in `framework/cli/build-engine.mjs`; engine-rpc `asset-templates`, console `GET /api/asset-templates?type=`. Empty list works end to end.

Validation in CI: `framework/spec/check-asset-templates.mjs` loads every template, runs `validateAsset`, checks unique ids, ≥ 10 per covered type once a type is marked `complete` in the index, and that each type has a `default`. Wire into `android.yml` (node job).

nav-menu ×10: side nav, bottom tabs, rail, grouped sections, icon-only, with badges, two-level, settings-first, admin, minimal. Each a valid `nav-menu` asset in `framework/assets/templates/nav-menu/`.
app-menu ×10 (file/edit/view style menus, single-page apps, tool apps…) + context-menu ×10 (text, list row, card, media, dev, file, link, minimal, with submenus, keyboard hints).
toolbar ×10: editor, media, search-first, compact icons, labelled, split start/end with widgets, status-heavy (counters/progress), collapsible, roomy, minimal.
layout ×10: dashboard, master-detail, sidebar-left/right, bottom-nav phone, kiosk, editor + inspector, chat, settings, full-bleed, three-pane. Each with `data.slots` where it narrows a region.
drawer ×10 (needs `asset-designer` step 7's `drawer` type): left/right, modal/non-modal, wide/narrow, with header, grouped, icon rail, account-first, admin, minimal.

color-theme ×10 light + ×10 dark (pairs): contrast-checked with `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks run from a script; names in one family (`arctic-daylight` style). Each pair shares a `pair` tag.
style-theme ×10: glass, flat, outlined, dense, roomy, rounded, square, hairline, soft, print. Numbers inside ranges known themes use; every opacity token present.

Defaults: `framework/defaults.json` + `framework/app-defaults.json` reviewed so every type has a default template id (new field `templates.default.<type>` read by `axf init` for "start from a template"); `axf init --template-set <id>` option registered in `build-options.json` only if it sets a token, else as an init argument.

Previews: `framework/cli/rebuild-shots.mjs`-style script `framework/cli/template-shots.mjs` renders each template in the demo app headless (phone + desktop) to `framework/assets/templates/<type>/shots/`; `index.json` entries get `shot`. Run once; commit shots ≤ 60 KB each (`framework/cli/shrink-shots.py`).

Android: templates bundled into `axf-assets` as a resource folder so Compose previews (`ComponentGallery.kt`) and the future Android designer read the same files; `AssetTemplates` Kotlin loader + a unit test that every bundled template validates.

Hooks: asset-designer "Start from" and Build Pilot's designers list templates by type (console `GET /api/asset-templates`); asset-browser shows a Templates source. Add the `templates` capability to `app-defaults` engine-rpc.
Close: regenerate fixtures touched (`gen-fixtures.mts`), CI green, report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-templates.md`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.templates` built, pending complete.

before.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
before.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. First real targets: xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite) and whatever claude-project parks.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: ask each time between the two ways.

steps.text: Spec first: `_claude/memory/docs/port-engine.md` — the two modes (bake / rebuild), the analysis report shape (`port-report@1`: stack, UI kit found, screens, chrome pieces → asset types, styles → tokens, libraries/plugins suggested, risk list), the staged codemod plan, and what `axf port` refuses (no manifest, dirty git tree). Read `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` and `claude-project.mjs` first.

CLI entry: `framework/cli/port.mjs` + `axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild [--report-only] [--stage N]` in `axf.mjs`; `requireProject` gate; refuses without `--yes` when git is dirty; writes `port-report.json` next to the manifest. `--report-only` works on an empty folder (empty report).

Stack detection: reuse `claude-project.mjs` detection (react/next/android/python…), add UI-kit detection (MUI, Chakra, shadcn, Material3, Compose, Tailwind) by package.json / gradle deps; unit test with fixture folders under `framework/spec/fixtures/port/`.

Analysis, screens + chrome: scan routes/screens (React Router / Next pages / Compose NavHost) and chrome components (app bar, drawer, bottom nav, menus, toolbars, dialogs) → candidate asset list with target type and confidence. Report section `pieces`.

Analysis, styles → tokens: run `portSource` from `ui-port.mjs` in dry mode over the codebase to count colour/size literals and role usages; map to the token list from the theme engine; report `tokens` with unmapped literals. Cap files scanned (size + count) and skip node_modules/build.

Bake, stage 1: `axf init` into the existing project (template by stack) without overwriting app files (`src/axf/` + assets + manifest relation `built-on`), `axf.lock.json`; app still builds (the template guard allows an existing codebase). Checked with a fixture react app.

Bake, stage 2: themes — generate `color-theme` + `style-theme` assets from the detected palette (nearest tokens), apply the literal → `var(--fx-*)` codemod (`ui-port.mjs portSource`) to CSS/TSX/Kotlin files in place with a `.port-backup/`; `--stage 2` only; report lists every file changed.

Bake, stage 3: chrome — generate nav-menu / app-menu / toolbar / dialog assets from the detected pieces and swap the components for the framework ones (`AppShell` / Compose `AppShell`), old components kept under `legacy/` until removed; `--stage 3`.

Rebuild mode: pick the closest boilerplate (`framework/boilerplates/index.json` tags vs detected features), `axf init --boilerplate` into `<dir>-axf` beside the old code, write `PORT-PLAN.md` with screen-by-screen mapping and the old file for each; report `rebuild.plan`.

Drivers: engine-rpc `port` / `port-report`, console `POST /api/port` + `GET /api/port/report?dir=`, MCP `app_port(dir, mode, stage)` (write, needs the console token); manifest `framework.relation` none → built-on when stage 1 runs (`project.mjs` validates).

Console view: Plugins → **Port** (or Wizards view section): pick a folder from allowed roots (project-wizard's `AXF_WIZARD_ROOTS` rule), run the report, show pieces/tokens tables, run stages one at a time with the file list and a diff count; rebuild plan rendered as a checklist.

Pending items hook: `port-<name>` items (parked by claude-project) get a "Run port" button in Pending rows (slot `pending.item`) that opens the console view on that project; `claude-project` writes `x.port.engine: "axf port"` into the manifest.
First real target, xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite): BRETT attaches the repo; run `--report-only`, review the report together, record the mode choice. No codemod yet.
xGallery bake stage 1–2 on a branch in that repo (init + themes), app builds; note unmapped literals; push branch `axf-port` for Brett to look at on the phone.
Tests: `framework/spec/check-port.mjs` over the fixture folders (detection, report shape, stage 1 idempotent, stage 2 backup + dry run, refusals: no manifest, dirty tree, symlinks); CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/app-port-engine.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status + `axf port` in Build/run/test, pending complete; decisions.md note on bake vs rebuild defaults.

before.title: lib-clone: any AXF app clones its own install with current data
before.detail:
Turn xGallery's New project wizard (MossesX/xGallery: server/src/routes/newproject.ts, src/pages/dev/newproject/NewProjectWizard.tsx, kit/new-project.mjs) into an AXF library so every app built on AXF can clone its install into a new project. Brett: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

What the xGallery wizard does today (reuse the design): renamed copy from the kit, GitHub repo, per-project deploy key installed on the VPS + Actions secrets (VPS_SSH_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN), Hostinger DNS for site + dev panel, Claude GitHub app access, push main, wait for the site deploy, push panel, wait, first-session prompt; resumable, no secrets stored.

New for the library: clone WITH current data (database snapshot + media/files, consistent copy, secrets and sessions stripped, owner reset), the copy gets its own project.manifest.json + _claude/ (claude-project), cross-port contract (web + Android) for the clone action exposed through the interop gate (default-deny), a settings tab (plugin manager rules: no own settings screen), console + MCP drivers. Open questions for Brett at build time: which data is copied by default, and whether the clone keeps users/members.

notes.text: Oct 18 2026: the project-creation half is built as the console plugin project-wizard (Opus): repo/folder/new AXF app → GitHub/VPS/local homes → manifest, _claude/, Claude.ai project kit, all on claude-project. lib-clone still covers the cross-port library and cloning an install WITH its data; reuse wizard.mjs for the homes and kit.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

steps.text: BRETT decides the two open questions before any code: (1) which data a clone copies by default (database snapshot + media? settings? sessions never), (2) whether users/members come along or the clone starts with the owner only. Write both into this item's notes and `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Contract `clone@1`: `framework/core/clone.ts` (TS reference) — `CloneRequest` {name, id, homes (github/vps/local like project-wizard), data: {database, media, settings, users}, stripSecrets: true}, `CloneReport`, pure validators (name/id rules from `claude-project.mjs`), exposure descriptor `clone.run` default-deny REMOTE (INTEROP.md). Fixture `spec/fixtures/clone.json` + `gen-fixtures`.

Kotlin mirror `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.clone` (same validators, `ConformanceTest` replay) + Python `framework/python/axf_libs/clone/contract.py` (used by server parts). Placeholder capability `axf.clone` declared in the kernel.

Library scaffold: `axf new-library clone --template service-provider --ports web,android,python` → `framework/libs/clone` (web `AxfWebLibrary` with a settings group "Clone", no own screen), `framework/android/lib-clone`, `framework/python/axf_libs/clone`; `axf compile-library clone` passes. Catalog `libraries.json` entry.

Data snapshot (server, Python): `axf_libs/clone/snapshot.py` — consistent copy of a SQLite db (`sqlite3 .backup`) and listed media folders into a temp dir, strip secret-looking files (reuse project-wizard's patterns), reset owner per the step-1 decision; unit test on a fixture db.

Homes + kit: reuse `apps/console-web/plugins/project-wizard/wizard.mjs` (`run`, `kit`, `link`) for GitHub/VPS/local homes, manifest, `_claude/`, Claude.ai kit; `clone` calls it with `source: folder` after the snapshot is unpacked into the new folder. One code path, no second copy of the wizard.

Web side: `framework/libs/clone/client.ts` (`CloneClient` over the app's API, token via a credential provider like `libs/mcp`), Settings → Clone group (name, id, data toggles from the decision, homes), progress stream (SSE like project-wizard), done screen with links. Gate: `rt.uac` must hold `clone.run`.

Android side: `lib-clone` `CloneModule` → Settings group + `CloneScreen` route `clone` calling the same API through axf-network; `AxfClone` registers the `axf.clone` provider; written without a compiler, CI `:lib-clone:testDebugUnitTest` with a fake server.

Console + MCP drivers: console plugin-free route `POST /api/clone` (admin only) running the Python engine; MCP `app_clone` (write, confirm required = destructive annotation); the console's own Settings → Plugins lists lib-clone like other libraries.

xGallery hook: xGallery keeps its wizard; add a `clone` endpoint there that imports `axf_libs.clone` (or calls the console API) so its New project wizard's "clone with data" uses the library — only after Brett attaches MossesX/xGallery.

Tests + CI: `framework/spec/check-clone.mts` (fixtures, validators), Python `axf_libs/clone/test.py` (snapshot strips secrets, resets owner, refuses symlinks/outside roots), lifecycle not needed (library). CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/lib-clone.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status, `libraries.json`/tracker, pending complete.

before.title: Agents + assistant sessions hosted on axHub (one host for every app)
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 20 2026: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

- axHub gets an agent + session host: runs turns, owns live-session@1 event logs (sessions survive app restarts and browser closes), per-agent memory, provider keys in axHub's vault, hub permissions for who may use which agent.
- Apps plug in through what the Fable rebuilds left open: the live-session host registry (`axf.live-host@1` / `register_host`, today a typed `axhub` placeholder in the console and Build Pilot), Build Pilot's assembly backend (BP_AGENT=local|console|off → add `axhub`), and the kernel placeholders `axf.agents`, `axhub.agent`.
- axHub never depends on AXF (decision): the host speaks the contracts over its API (AXPP), with an AXF adapter on the AXF side (lib-hub).
- The assembly gate (pilot-assembly@1) stays in Build Pilot: axHub only proposes ops; Build Pilot checks and builds. Manual mode unaffected.
- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

Until then: Build Pilot runs its agent locally (Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026), the console's assistant hosts its own sessions.

notes.text: Nov 3 2026: s12 (Build Pilot backend) skipped, Build Pilot is retired.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

steps.text: BRETT attaches MossesX/axHub. Read its session/worker layout, decisions #70–#87 and the AXPP protocol doc; write `_claude/memory/docs/axhub-agent-host.md` design: host API (sessions, turns, events, agents, memory, permissions), where provider keys live (vault, write-only), what the AXF adapter translates. No code.

Protocol contract (AXF side, pure): `framework/core/live-session.ts` gains the wire shape for a remote host (`RemoteHostDescriptor`, event envelope with seq, resume cursor), fixtures in `spec/fixtures/live-session.json` → `remote`; Kotlin `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.live` + Python mirror replay them.

axHub, session store: `sessions` table/collection (id, owner, agent, created, closed, cursor) + append-only event log keyed by seq (file or db per axHub's storage), with replay from a cursor; unit tests.

axHub, turn runner: a worker that runs one turn for a session (provider call through axHub's existing LLM client or a new one using vault keys), streams events into the log, survives the browser going away; one running turn per session; stop/cancel.

axHub, agents: `agent-definition@1` validator ported from `framework/core/agents.ts` (fixture `agents.json` replayed), agent registry per project in `/projects/<name>/_data/agents/`, per-agent memory using the memory engine rules from the contract.

axHub, permissions: who may use which agent / open sessions / write mode, as hub user permissions (`agents.use.<id>`, `sessions.open`, `agents.write`) on the users page, enforced on every host route; admin bypass as elsewhere on the hub.

axHub, host API: `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}/turns` (POST = run), `/sessions/{id}/events?since=` (SSE + replay), `/sessions/{id}/stop|close`; approvals for destructive tool calls through the hub's approval screen (one-tap link rule). OpenAPI snippet in the design doc.

axHub, provider keys: turns use keys from the vault by name (`llm.<provider>`), never returned; `vault.set` from the console's Keys needed flow already exists — add the names to the systems-check key list on the AXF side later (step 15).

AXF adapter, web: `framework/libs/hub` (lib-hub, first slice exists) gets `AxhubLiveHost implements SessionHost` over the host API with the hub session cookie / token provider; registers through `axf.live-sessions@1.register_host()`; the console's AI assistant picks it when Settings → Assistant → Host = axHub.

AXF adapter, Android: `lib-hub` Kotlin `AxhubLiveHost` over axf-network (SSE reader from `lib-mcp`'s parser), registered in the kernel's live-session host registry; placeholder `axhub.agent` becomes real; written without a compiler, CI unit test with MockWebServer.

Console assistant on the hub host: `ai-assistant` plugin `server/sessions.py` host `axhub` stops being a `PlaceholderHost`: a thin proxy host that forwards to the hub API with the signed-in user's identity; reconnect/replay through the existing `watchReply` fold; `test.py` cases with a fake hub.

Build Pilot: `BP_AGENT=axhub` backend in `server/assembly.py` calling the hub host for the `pilot-assembler` agent; the assembly gate (`pilot-assembly@1`) still checks every op locally; manual mode untouched; `test_server.py` with a fake hub.
Phone apps: the AXHub Android app gets a Sessions tab (list, attach to a live reply, stop) on `lib-hub`'s host client; the Android console's assistant screen (when it exists) uses the same.

Migration: console sessions stored locally can be exported/imported into the hub (`POST /sessions/import` with the event log); one-time "Move my sessions to axHub" button in the assistant settings; no data loss on failure (import is additive).
Systems check: new checks `axhub-agent-host` (host reachable, caller allowed) and the vault key names for providers in the Keys needed list; Auto fix opens the right pages.
Alerts + activity: hub sessions appear in the Activity banner source list (`axf.activity@1`), failed turns raise an alert via the hub → console alerts source `axhub`.
Tests, AXF side: `check-live-session` fixture cases for the remote shape, lib-hub web unit tests (fake SSE), Android unit test, plugin `test.py` additions; CI lines in `android.yml`.
Tests, axHub side: host API tests (permissions, replay from cursor, one turn per session, stop), agent validator fixture replay, vault key never returned.

Deploy: axHub redeploy on Coolify with the worker enabled (env for worker count), console `install-console.sh` passes `AXF_ASSISTANT_HOST=axhub` once the hub answers; BRETT approves the deploy and runs one turn from his phone.
Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/axhub-agent-host.md`, LOG.md, decisions.md (#88+ on the hub side), CLAUDE.md Status in both repos, pending complete.

steps.text: BRETT attaches MossesX/axHub. Read its session/worker layout, decisions #70–#87 and the AXPP protocol doc; write `_claude/memory/docs/axhub-agent-host.md` design: host API (sessions, turns, events, agents, memory, permissions), where provider keys live (vault, write-only), what the AXF adapter translates. No code.

Protocol contract (AXF side, pure): `framework/core/live-session.ts` gains the wire shape for a remote host (`RemoteHostDescriptor`, event envelope with seq, resume cursor), fixtures in `spec/fixtures/live-session.json` → `remote`; Kotlin `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.live` + Python mirror replay them.

axHub, session store: `sessions` table/collection (id, owner, agent, created, closed, cursor) + append-only event log keyed by seq (file or db per axHub's storage), with replay from a cursor; unit tests.

axHub, turn runner: a worker that runs one turn for a session (provider call through axHub's existing LLM client or a new one using vault keys), streams events into the log, survives the browser going away; one running turn per session; stop/cancel.

axHub, agents: `agent-definition@1` validator ported from `framework/core/agents.ts` (fixture `agents.json` replayed), agent registry per project in `/projects/<name>/_data/agents/`, per-agent memory using the memory engine rules from the contract.

axHub, permissions: who may use which agent / open sessions / write mode, as hub user permissions (`agents.use.<id>`, `sessions.open`, `agents.write`) on the users page, enforced on every host route; admin bypass as elsewhere on the hub.

axHub, host API: `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}/turns` (POST = run), `/sessions/{id}/events?since=` (SSE + replay), `/sessions/{id}/stop|close`; approvals for destructive tool calls through the hub's approval screen (one-tap link rule). OpenAPI snippet in the design doc.

axHub, provider keys: turns use keys from the vault by name (`llm.<provider>`), never returned; `vault.set` from the console's Keys needed flow already exists — add the names to the systems-check key list on the AXF side later (step 15).

AXF adapter, web: `framework/libs/hub` (lib-hub, first slice exists) gets `AxhubLiveHost implements SessionHost` over the host API with the hub session cookie / token provider; registers through `axf.live-sessions@1.register_host()`; the console's AI assistant picks it when Settings → Assistant → Host = axHub.

before.title: UI-kit switching + fallback
before.detail: Every component is an abstract kind; the active ui-kit asset picks which library renders it. Kinds a kit lacks fall back to the default AmberX kit and are noted on the output terminal.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web kit contract: `framework/core/uikit.ts` = Kotlin `contract/UiKit.kt` (`ComponentKind` list from `ui-port.mjs` `COMPONENT_KINDS`, `UiKitSpec`, `UiKitResolver` with fallback to the default AmberX kit + terminal note per missing kind); fixture `spec/fixtures/uikit.json` (resolve, fallback, note text).

React kit registry: `framework/react/kits/index.ts` with the built-in `amberx` kit (today's components mapped by kind) and `registerKit(spec, impl)`; `AppShell`/`Controls` resolve each kind through the resolver instead of importing components directly.

ui-kit asset wiring: the active `ui-kit` asset (already an asset type on Android) picks the kit on web too; Settings → Appearance → UI kit drop-down (both ports share the setting key); rolls exclude it (`rollDefaults.never`).

Second kit (proof): `framework/libs/kit-mui` skeleton via `axf new-library kit-mui --template ui-kit --ports web` with 6 kinds (BUTTON, TEXT_FIELD, SWITCH, CARD, DIALOG, TOAST) on MUI reading only `--fx-*` tokens (THEMING.md); missing kinds fall back and are listed in the Output terminal.
Kotlin parity check: `UiKitConformanceTest` replaying `uikit.json` against `UiKitResolver`; `check-theme.mjs` covers `libs/kit-*`.
Python placeholder: `framework/python/axf/uikit.py` resolver replaying the fixture (Qt Widgets kit stays planned, a placeholder capability `axf.uikit.qt`).
Docs + status: PORTING.md "UI kits", plan web → built, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Libraries: settings, logging, admin, accounts, profile, billing
before.detail: The six libraries the console and apps build on. Settings and logging are complete; accounts and billing run on mock providers.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Scope note first: `_claude/memory/docs/libs-core.md` — for each of admin, accounts, profile, billing: what the Android placeholder has (`lib-admin`, `lib-accounts`, `lib-profile`, `lib-billing` screens + modules), what "real" means per port (accounts = axHub provider from `x.session`; billing = provider interface only, Play Billing as a separate library per the plan's recommendation), the web library ids (`ai.amberx.axf.<name>`).

Web lib-logging: `framework/libs/logging` (`AxfWebLibrary`: log sinks via `ExtensionPoints.LOG_SINKS`, levels, the Output terminal as default sink, Settings → General → Logging group) matching `lib-logging` on Android; `axf init` web templates install it beside settings.

Web lib-accounts: `framework/libs/accounts` (Account view = today's `react/studio/AccountView.tsx` moved into the library, sign-in/out through `rt.session` providers, Settings → Account group); the console installs it.

Android lib-accounts real: `AccountsModule` consumes `AUTH_PROVIDERS` (from `x.session` step 4), `AccountScreen` shows the provider's principal, sign-in/out, errors; mock provider moved to `lib-accounts-mock`; `lib-accounts` unit test with a fake provider.

Profile: `lib-profile` Android (`ProfileScreen` edits display name/avatar stored per principal in KV, exported through a `ProfileProvider` interface) + web `framework/libs/profile` (same provider interface, avatar widget uses `avatar` widget kind); contract in `core/profile.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Profile.kt`.

Admin: `lib-admin` Android + web `framework/libs/admin`: an admin-only view (UAC `admin.*`) listing modules/libraries (plugin-inventory), audit log, flags toggles (`x.state` flags), feature kill switches; hidden entirely without the role.

Billing: provider contract `core/billing.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Billing.kt` (products, entitlements, purchase flow result, restore), `BILLING_PROVIDERS` typed; `lib-billing` Android with a `NoBilling` provider (entitlements empty) and `SubscriptionScreen` driven by the provider; web `framework/libs/billing` same; Play Billing library parked as a plan feature (`x.lib.billing.play`).
Fixtures + Kotlin tests: `spec/fixtures/libs-core.json` (profile validation, billing entitlement rules, admin role gate) replayed on both ports; written without a compiler.
Templates: `axf init` installs logging + accounts + profile on web/Android by default (settings already is), build options unchanged; CI template sweep + `axf validate` on the generated apps.

Catalog + status: `libraries.json` entries for the six on web/android/python(planned), status.json features `a.admin`, `u.accounts`, `p.profile`, `b.subs` → built (billing = contract + NoBilling), tracker, `build_step complete`.
Console: Settings → Account & security uses lib-accounts/profile; Standards → nothing changes; console tsc + vite build; theme-swap script passes on the new views.
Docs: PORTING.md "Core libraries", CLAUDE.md Status bullet, `_claude/memory/docs/libs-core.md` finished with what stayed placeholder (Play Billing).

before.title: Import third-party UI libraries → AmberX kits
before.detail: axf import-ui clones (git/local) or records (maven/npm) a library, rewrites literals and Material/MUI roles to AXF tokens, saves kit-<id> + its ui-kit asset and applies it to the open project.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Real-library trial: run `axf import-ui --name Cupertino --kit cupertino --source git --path <compose-cupertino repo>` into a scratch android-compose app (`/tmp`), read `tokens.map.json`, list what the codemod missed (patterns + counts) in `_claude/memory/docs/uiport-trial.md`.

Codemod fixes from the trial: extend `ROLE_MAP`/`guessToken` in `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` for the missed Compose patterns (e.g. `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.x`, `Modifier.padding(Nn.dp)` → space tokens), unit cases in `framework/spec/check-uiport.mjs` (new; fixture snippets in `spec/fixtures/uiport/`).

Kit overrides: generated `kit-<id>` module gets per-kind override files from the library's components (mapping table in `tokens.map.json` → `components.map.json`), default components kept where unmapped; the ui-kit asset lists `covers`.
Web side: `import-ui` for npm libraries (MUI first) generating `framework/libs/kit-<id>` from the `ui-kit` library template with the same maps; `check-theme.mjs` passes on the output.
CI + status: `check-uiport.mjs` in `android.yml` (node job) + the existing fake-lib import sweep; plan warnings cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Live reload (axf dev) + device hot reload
before.detail: axf dev watches assets and long-polls changes to devices; the Android HotReloader re-registers changed assets live.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web hot reload: `framework/react` `useDevServer(url)` long-polls `/events` from `dev-server.mjs` and re-registers changed assets (`registry.register` + `rt.refreshFromSaved`); `axf dev` prints the URL; demo app opts in with `?axfDev=`.

Android end to end on the emulator (CI): `rebuild-shots.yml`-style job step that starts `axf dev --framework` on the runner, points the emulator at `10.0.2.2:7070` (setting `axf.devServer`, flag `axf.hotReload`), edits a theme file, screenshots before/after and asserts the pixel diff > 0.

Robustness: dev server validates every changed file before announcing it (invalid → `/events` carries `error` and the device shows a terminal line), ignores editor temp files, handles rename/delete; `check-dev-server.mjs` test with a temp folder.
Docs + status: README section "Live reload on a phone" (PC IP, same Wi-Fi), plan warning cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Session, principal, audit log
before.detail: Session/Principal/SessionProvider contracts and an AuditLog service; accounts library uses a mock auth provider.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web contract: `framework/core/session.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Session.kt` (`Principal`, `Session`, `SessionState`, `SessionProvider`, `AnonymousSession`, `AuditEntry`, `AuditLog`, `MemoryAuditLog`); `rt.session` replaces the ad-hoc principal in `runtime.ts` (`bindPrincipal` keeps working, built on it); fixture `spec/fixtures/session.json` (state transitions, audit cap).

Audit log everywhere: every UAC-denied action, swap, settings write of a locked key and bound-principal refusal records an `AuditEntry` (web + Kotlin, same action names); Settings → Account & security → **Audit** list (last 100) in `libs/settings` and Android `SettingsScreen`.

Real provider, axHub: `lib-hub` gets `AxhubSessionProvider` (web: `/api/me` + hub cookie; Android: the AXHub app's cookie-jar sign-in) mapping hub role/perms → `Principal`; the console's `account.tsx` reads `rt.session` instead of its own fetch; first non-mock provider.

Kotlin: `AuthProviders` extension point typed (`AUTH_PROVIDERS` → `SessionProvider`), `lib-accounts` picks the first registered provider (mock stays as fallback module `lib-accounts-mock`); `SessionConformanceTest` replays the fixture; written without a compiler.

Persistence: session survives restart (Kotlin KV `<key>:session` minus secrets; web settings), `EXPIRED`/`LOCKED` transitions on expiry and app lock (lib-lock hooks `LOCKED`); fixture cases for expiry.
Tests + CI: `check-session.mts`, Kotlin test, console `test_wall_users.py` unchanged; CI lines.
Docs + status: PORTING.md "Session + audit", plan android/web partial → built, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`; warning "No real sign-in provider yet" cleared.

before.title: Python / PyQt6 port
before.detail: Port the kernel engines to Python, pass the conformance fixtures, add a PyQt6 UI layer, a Qt Widgets kit and a pyqt6 app template.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Plan the port (no code): `_claude/memory/docs/python-port.md` — engines in fixture order (theme → layout → components → UAC → actions → hide/spacing/roll/search → banner/widgets), package layout `framework/python/axf/engines/`, dataclasses mirroring the Kotlin models, how fixtures are replayed (`framework/python/axf/spec/replay.py`), what the PyQt6 layer covers in the first slice.

Fixture replay harness: `framework/python/axf/spec/replay.py` loads every `spec/fixtures/*.json`, dispatches by fixture name to a registered engine, reports pass/fail per case; CI job `python-port` runs it (allowed to skip unported engines, listed).
Asset model + validator: `axf/asset.py` (envelope dataclass, `validate_asset` from `asset-types.json` incl. `attach`/`widgets` hosts, slot checks) replaying `validation.json`.
Theme engine: `axf/engines/theme.py` (color + style compile, spacing scale, opacity tokens) replaying `theme.json` + `spacing.json`.
Layout engine: `axf/engines/layout.py` (`compile_slots`, `region_accepts`, hidden regions) replaying `layout.json`, `layout-slots.json`, `hide.json`.
Components engine: `axf/engines/components.py` (component styles, toolbar/nav/app-menu style inputs, container collapsible, toolbar collapsible) replaying `components.json`.
UAC + actions: `axf/engines/uac.py`, `actions.py` replaying `uac.json`, `actions.json`, `menu-filter.json`.
Roll + search engines: `axf/engines/roll.py`, `search.py` replaying `roll.json`, `search.json`.
Banner + widgets engines: `axf/engines/banner.py`, `widgets.py` (host registry, kinds rules) replaying `banner.json`, `widgets.json`.
Runtime: `axf/runtime.py` (registry, swap, settings store, hidden slots, attachments, bound principal, session from `x.session`) with the same action ids; smoke test registering the starter assets.
Project gate: `axf/project.py` validator replaying `project-manifest.json` (same rules file), used by the pyqt6 template's guard.

PyQt6 shell, part 1: `axf/qt/shell.py` — window with banner, menubar (app-menu), toolbar, nav (side list), content region from the compiled layout; theme tokens → Qt stylesheet via a token→QSS compiler.
PyQt6 shell, part 2: dialogs/popups, context menu, settings window driven by `SettingsGroup`s (lib-settings python), search bar widget, clock widget; hot-swap re-applies QSS live.
Qt Widgets kit: `axf/qt/kit.py` implementing the `ComponentKind` table on QtWidgets through the uikit resolver (`x.uikits` python placeholder becomes real).

Template `pyqt6`: `framework/templates/pyqt6` (`template.json`, `project.manifest.json`, `main.py`, `requirements.txt`, guard), `axf init --template pyqt6` wired in `build-engine.mjs` (bakes `framework/python/axf` + assets); `axf validate` on the output.
Tests + CI: replay harness must pass every fixture (no skips left), `python -m pytest framework/python` job, template sweep includes pyqt6 (no display: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` smoke).
Docs + status: PORTING.md "Python port", plan python ports → built across epics touched, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`; `axf init` README lists the template.

before.title: Plugin runtime (deliver features after install)
before.detail: plugin@1 manifest, scopes, action macros and a PluginLoader contract exist; loading plugins at runtime is a placeholder.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Design check (no code): read `contract/Plugin.kt` (PACK/MODULE/SCRIPT, scopes, `PluginLoader`), `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json` if asset-browser made it, and the plugin-catalog format; write `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-runtime.md`: what a PACK may carry (assets, action macros, string packs), install sources (file, URL, QR, console catalog), grants UI, and what stays placeholder (MODULE code loading, SCRIPT).

Pack format on every port: `framework/schemas/plugin-pack.json` (`pack@1`: manifest plugin@1 + files list + hashes) validated by TS (`core/plugins-pack.ts`), Kotlin (`PluginManifest` + pack reader) and Python (catalog engine); fixture `spec/fixtures/plugin-pack.json` (good pack, over-scope pack refused, bad hash).

Android loader, PACK only: `axf-platform-android` `PackLoader implements PluginLoader` — stage from file/URL (OkHttp, no redirects, size cap), verify hashes, keep under `filesDir/plugins/<id>/`, states STAGED→DISABLED→ENABLED; `axf.plugins` placeholder replaced for PACK, MODULE/SCRIPT still answer NotImplemented.

Android apply: an enabled pack registers its assets into `AssetRegistry` (origin = plugin id, conflicts reported as diagnostics) and its macros into `ExtensionPoints.MACROS`; disable/uninstall removes exactly those; unit test with a fixture pack.

before.title: Console in its own private repo
before.detail: Split apps/console-web into a private repo that depends on a tagged framework version.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: BRETT says go (rule: not until he does) and picks the dependency style: tagged framework version via git tag + `npm pack`-style tarball, or a git submodule. Record in decisions.md.

Framework packaging: `framework/cli/axf.mjs pack-framework <tag>` producing `axf-framework-<tag>.tgz` (core, react, ui, schemas, libs, plan cores) + a GitHub release asset on tag push (`release.yml`).

Repo split: create `MossesX/axf-console` (exists on GitHub first), move `apps/console-web` with history (`git subtree split`), manifest `location` + `repo.exists: true`, `_claude/` + CLAUDE.md via `claude-project`; CI there re-bakes from the tagged tarball instead of `../../framework`.

This repo: `apps/console-web` becomes a thin pointer (README + manifest `location` pointing at the new repo), `install-console.sh` clones the console repo; `deploy/` scripts and `android.yml` console job updated.
Verify: console builds in its repo against the tag, deploy on the VPS from the new clone, `/api/health` + `/mcp` ok; status + `build_step complete`.

before.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

origin.brief:
# GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/github-app.md: what Brett taps, where things are stored (paths only), what now uses the app.

steps.text: Token broker (framework/cli/github-app.mjs + github-token.mjs): manifest, conversion, JWT, installation + user tokens, cache, lock
git credential helper + gh wrapper + repo create
Console plugin github-app: routes, keeper, health checks, settings UI
Point callers at the broker (key check on old token, push-banner probe)
Tests, screenshots, install_steps, report, push
