before.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

before.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.

origin.brief:
# GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/github-app.md: what Brett taps, where things are stored (paths only), what now uses the app.

steps.text: Token broker (framework/cli/github-app.mjs + github-token.mjs): manifest, conversion, JWT, installation + user tokens, cache, lock
git credential helper + gh wrapper + repo create
Console plugin github-app: routes, keeper, health checks, settings UI
Point callers at the broker (key check on old token, push-banner probe)
Tests, screenshots, install_steps, report, push

before.title: Automated Browser plugin (drive, record, edit, schedule)
before.detail: Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice), verbatim: "Make me a plugin that shows a browser that can be driven by the app, give it the ability to be automated and to record automation routines through the browser, like make it record in real time what you do and save the events, so you can redo everything that you just recorded, and have a powerful editor to see what each step is doing. Make it so that you can create workflows through the automated browser and record the steps, or do them automatically and record as you go, or record manually, and full powerful editing, able to tweak the JavaScript and whatever you gotta do to make it follow a routine, like go to a site and log in, or go to a site and go to a products page and grab something, and then have a scheduler built into it that you can schedule when to perform these routines." Addendum: "Be able to manually record, or tell you to do it, so it needs to be integrated with the assistant or with its own access to the assistant." Browser runs on the VPS (Playwright + headless Chromium), live view over CDP screencast; REST + MCP + CLI; secrets by vault reference only. Booked to Snap Sully (no Polo card).

steps.text: Browser host: Node Playwright service (sessions, tabs, persisted profile per workspace, navigate/back/forward/reload, device size, CDP screencast + input over websocket, downloads, screenshot, extract) + tests
Plugin server part: FastAPI routes proxying the host (REST), websocket relay, plugin.json, install/uninstall, health check in Systems check
Live view UI: URL bar, back/forward/reload, tabs, phone/desktop size, zoom, canvas with click/type/scroll forwarding (framework controls, tokens only)
CLI + MCP tools for driving (open, navigate, click, type, screenshot, extract, tabs) + container/service deploy for the host on the VPS
routine@1 asset type contract: asset-types.json entry, validator, routine engine (step model, selectors, variables, loops/conditions, extract, vault refs), fixture, starter asset
Recorder: in-page capture of navigate/click/type/select/scroll/wait/upload into routine@1 steps with selector candidates (role/text/test-id, CSS fallback) + thumbnails; password masking
Replay runner: run all, step-by-step, run from here, highlight current step in the live view, waits/retries/timeouts, vault refs resolved at run time
Routine editor UI: step list (type, target, value, wait, retries, timeout, screenshot), edit/reorder/disable/duplicate, variables
Editor: loops/conditions (if exists, for each), Extract steps (text, attribute, table, list -> JSON/CSV)
JavaScript editor per step + routine (highlight, run-in-page, console output) + selector picker from the live view
Test run with per-step pass/fail and diff of results against the last run
Scheduler engine: once / every N / daily / weekly / cron, America/New_York, enable/pause, run now, retries, max concurrent, time limits (framework work scheduler contract)
Scheduler UI + run history (logs, screenshots, extracted data) + notify on fail/result (banner/push)
Assistant panel docked beside the live view: chat drives the browser via tools and records each step as it goes, narrates; take over by hand and hand back
Assistant edits/explains/fixes routines and creates schedules; MCP tools for record/routines/schedules so Amber and Gizmo can do it from their chats
Starter routines (log in, grab a product's price on toscrape test sites), tests, phone + desktop shots, UI Review, report (cost, Chromium memory), THREADS, PR

before.title: App style override: axHub is the style source, per-app Override design / colors, reload + save to axHub
before.detail: What Brett said (Nov 3 2026, voice): "Put a button in each app's settings to override axHub's style, in design and colors." Addendum 1: "And the hook will reload axHub, and you can also save design back to axHub." Context: axHub defines the default look for every app; apps inherit it live; manual edits override per setting with an 'Overriding axHub' note (same rule as molly-nav-submenus Addendum 6 and gizmo-companion's appearance add-on). Agent: Ping Paulie (no Polo card). Model: Opus for every step (Claude decides); additive web-only contract, Android twin deferred in PORTING.md; Fable review recommended per the shared rule.

notes.text: Reconciler: PR #302
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: s1 axHub = style source: axHub's active color-theme + style-theme is the default for every app (console, Molly, axHub web, AmberX, demo, Gizmo later, framework app template); inheriting apps follow it live

s2 Settings > Appearance in each app: Override axHub design / Override axHub colors switches, Inherited from axHub note with theme name, Overriding axHub with axHub value beside, auto-on when editing, Reset to axHub
s3 Shared inherit/override library in the framework (reuse molly-nav-submenus if it made one)
s4 Banner tokens: per-banner-type colour tokens (info, success, warning, error, build, merge, ai, neutral) in color-theme with values in every starter theme
s5 Addendum 1: Reload from axHub (button + hook@1 action, keep or reset overrides) and Save to axHub (design / colours / both, confirm lists apps, owner-only, versioned, Restore previous axHub style)
s6 REST + MCP + CLI (app_style_get, app_style_override, app_style_reload, app_style_save_to_axhub), tests, screenshots, UI Review, report, THREADS, PR

before.title: Fable review: Opus-built foundation work, Nov 3-4
before.detail: Read-and-fix review on Fable of foundation work built on Opus on Nov 3-4 2026 (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines, cross-app protocols). For each: read the contract, engine, fixtures and validators; fix what is wrong or unsafe to build on; keep everything else. Fixes go through one PR and merge when green. Report _claude/builds/reports/fable-review-nov3.md (what was checked, what changed, what was fine).

notes.text: model-thinking-audit (Nov 4): the audit list is in _claude/builds/reports/model-thinking-audit.md and on every build (node framework/cli/model-advice.mjs audit --json; filter 'Fable candidates'). Consume it from there. s2 (plugin-settings-placement): the settings-placement@1 Fable review already ran as settings-placement-everywhere s2 (Fable, same PR #329), so s2 can be ticked against it. Top redo picks: orch-live-sync, pass-all, requests-ledger, settings-asset / appearance-asset-tokens (their parked -fable twins are the redo).
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: I don't want the approvals. Just put everything that needs to be on Fable on Fable. No more approvals. If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable. And what about yesterday? Was anything that needed to be Fable done with Opus?

steps.text: banner-ref-links (#287): ref@1 matching rules (cross-app GUI behaviour contract); review + fix
plugin-settings-placement (#289): settings-placement@1 contract; review + fix
molly-console-commands (#288): Molly <-> app messages (embed@1 front messages addition); review + fix
molly-nav-submenus (#295): nav-style contract (report asks for a Fable review); review + fix
smart-menus (#281): smart-menu engine contract review; plus the menu-style asset type (Addendum 3) that was skipped because a new asset type needed an upgrade approval
crew-live (parked part): avatar 'agent' source asset-type change; design + build it
Report fable-review-nov3.md, tests, PR (merges when green)

# Build: molly-banner-match

## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-04T15:25:00Z
> Make Molly's top banner asset the same as console. And when console's open in Molly, don't display its own banner.

## What to build
Continue build "Molly's banner = the console's banner asset; embedded apps hide their own" (molly-banner-match) [Molly] — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (voice, 2026-11-04 15:25):
"Make Molly's top banner asset the same as console. And when console's open in Molly, don't display its own banner."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

before.title: Planner: select items and build them
before.detail: In Plan Studio, select any parts (single steps or features at any depth, or the whole plan) with multi-select, then click Create build to make one build from the selection.

notes.text: Brett: "Without AI." Select and create build must work with no AI: plain UI that assembles the brief from the selected items directly.

Brett: "So whenever you plan something, it gets a file that writes out what it would prompt AI to say. What it would tell you, but it doesn't say anything until you, unless you add it to a new build." Every plan item has a stored, prewritten prompt file. Nothing is sent to AI until the selection is added to a new build, and then those prompts make up the brief.

Brett: "You can view that file through hooks, the theater. The different steps, maybe the context menu. Or you can do multiple selection, make them rebuild and view the prompt that it generates. Without AI." The prompt file can be viewed per step (theater/hover view, context menu). Multi-select, then rebuild or preview the generated prompt before sending. All of it without AI.

Brett: progress tracking applies to ALL builds, not only ones started from the planner (builds already split into steps). Every build_start brief includes the check-off instruction, and the console reads the progress live for every build. Resume from the first unchecked step.

Re-added (lost in an overwrite): (a) AmberX task and checklist rows: click a row to see the text discussed; expandable rows show amendments; send a row straight to its own new build. (b) A build from the planner auto-ticks items as it finishes them; the brief lists the item IDs and tells it to tick them. (c) The console tracks progress live without AI, through the console API or a progress file in the build dir; no stopping or resending context; if a build dies, the next run resumes at the first unchecked item.

CORRECTION from Brett: the build manager already tracks build progress, so drop the console-tracking and progress-file notes above. NEW: every build (anything Amber or anyone starts) automatically creates a plan in Plan Studio and goes into a build registry. That plan uses the same steps the build manager will use, so they stay in sync (one source of truth) and tick off together, along with the linked AmberX checklist rows. Registry and planner are categorized by app, plugin, edit, feature, in collapsible trees with sorting and filters.
Brett: the build manager and the planner both read and write progress in the SAME registry, one source of truth, with no separate copies to sync.

Brett: backfill the registry: import every existing build (the 79 finished-but-not-landed, the running/queued ones, and landed ones, going back as far as the history goes) as plans with their steps and status, read from the build dirs, briefs, logs, and git branches.
Brett: each registry/plan entry shows its addenda and amendments: every later change, note, or restart (e.g. r2/r3 runs), in order with timestamps, in expandable rows. Backfill them too.

OVERLAP: token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control steps 14-15 (orchestrator IDs/registry), 26-29 (parked plans, multi-select, right-click new build, checklist grid) cover much of this. Prompt-file/preview parts not covered.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

# Build: Headless progress file + lean CLAUDE.md chain
Orchestrator build id: headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain (planner.builds). Follow the CLAUDE.md chain and rules as usual.

Goal: headless sessions never stop to update the console; they write progress to a small file the console reads. Cut tokens spent on the CLAUDE.md chain.

Steps (each ~10 min, commit after each):
1. Define progress file format + location per build (current step, status, last update, notes).
2. Headless runner (deploy/claude-headless.sh etc.): write/update progress file after each step without pausing. Use it yourself in this build from step 2 on.
3. Orchestrator: include progress file in every new build on registration.
4. Console: read progress file on demand and show where the build is.
5. Remove old stop-to-update-console behavior from headless sessions.
6. Audit the CLAUDE.md chain headless sessions load (files, size, tokens per step).
7. Headless: load a slim build brief instead of full chain; pull rules files only when a step needs them.
8. Load chain once per session, not every step; verify.

Tick each step done in the orchestrator as you go. Finish with README/help update, report, PR to merge queue.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

origin.brief:
# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

origin.brief:
# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

One session, lean chain.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need a really sweet interface for the scheduling stuff, the schedules. Make it sick."
- Polished, modern calendar UI (framework tokens + theme only): smooth view transitions, drag to create / move / resize events, colour-coded calendars, now-line, mini-month, quick-add bar (plain English: 'gym every Mon Wed 6pm'), weekly schedule editor with drag blocks, phone gestures (swipe days/weeks, long-press drag), dark/light. Phone-first, desktop great too.
- Screenshots of every view (phone + desktop) to UI Review.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Open that in its own window with multiple layouts. Open numerous schedules, days and weeks: a week here and a month there, and drag events from here to there. Attach an RSVP list / invite list to an event with a check mark of who's replied. Send automatic emails to RSVP people, or emails asking people to confirm they've read/seen it. It needs to update in the scheduler on AmberX."
- Calendar opens in its own window (windows@1 / dock@1); multiple panes side by side, each any view/date/calendar; save named layouts; drag events between panes.
- Invite / RSVP list per event: guests, status (invited / yes / no / maybe / seen), check marks, counts. Emails sent through axHub Google (Gmail) when it exists: invites, automatic RSVP reminders, read/seen confirmation requests (tracked link). Replies update the event status live on console and AmberX. Sending email = confirm approval (axHub policy).

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"Any replies to the emails get logged. They type their reply in a text field that's sent in the email; they have to reply in the text field so it gets logged in the system."
- Each invite/reminder email has a link to a small public reply page (per-guest signed token, no login): RSVP buttons + a text field. Submissions are logged on the event (who, when, answer, message) and update status live on console + AmberX.
- Plain email replies are also caught via Gmail (axHub) and logged on the event when possible, but the reply page is the main path.
- Reply page is rate-limited, token expires, no other data exposed.

# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

origin.brief:
# Postgres: ONE true location for all data sets, in its own container (Brett, Nov 7)

Orchestrator build id: `postgres-console` (profile all, 7 steps) with Plan Studio plan `postgres-for-the-console-orchestrator-id-registr-anyx` — read both (`node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs brief postgres-console`) and follow them, with this change: Postgres runs in its OWN Docker container, not inside the console's.

Problem: the same data lives in 3+ places (builds store, per-profile orchestrator files, pending list, journal, plans, tracker/catalog, feature-ledger, origins) read by different tools, constantly out of sync.

1. Contract (Fable): schema for builds, steps, plans, blueprints, journal, queue, accounts/workers usage, Shipped features, origins, ID registry (orchestrator assigns every id). Migrations versioned.
2. Own container: `axf-postgres` (official image, pinned), internal Docker network only (no public port), named data volume, healthcheck, restart policy, nightly backup + restore script, credentials in the vault/env (never in git). Compose/deploy files + docs.
3. Importer: every existing JSON source loaded losslessly, counts/hashes verified, duplicates resolved with a report.
4. Switch every reader/writer (orchestrator, Build manager, Builds page, Plan Studio, builds-live, merge queue, MCP/CLI, AmberX, axHub) to the DB. JSON files become generated read-only exports for git/sessions. Kill file locks.
5. CI check: no code writes those JSON files directly anymore.
6. Tests + perf check. Add to Shipped features.

Deploying the container is a VPS write: prepare it, and leave a one-command deploy for Brett/orchestrator. Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push.

steps.text: Schema + contract: builds, steps, plans, plan steps, IDs registry, pending ids, changes, journal, queue, origins, token log
Migration design: import every JSON file losslessly, dual-write period, rollback, JSON exports stay generated read-only for git/claude-sync
Bundle Postgres into the console container with data on a persistent volume (survives redeploys), backups
Orchestrator is the ID registry: planner requests IDs, orchestrator assigns + registers build ID and pending ID
Switch readers/writers over (Build manager, orchestrator, Plan Studio, to-do sync, Codebase changes, MCP/CLI); kill file locks, use transactions
Query screen in the console (read-only queries, saved queries)
Tests, perf check, docs

before.title: Patches/AmberX redesign: 8 game-style PREVIEWS for UI Review (no build until pick)
before.detail: Rebuild the entire AmberX UI (app and console) from scratch, ignoring the current look. Overall direction: make it look really good, like a polished Windows PC game UI — game-launcher / game-menu feel, rich depth, glow, motion, HUD-style panels, bold typography. Produce 8 distinct concepts within that game direction, each with its own style, colour theme and layout (e.g. sci-fi HUD, fantasy RPG menu, cyberpunk neon, racing/sports dashboard, tactical military, sleek AAA launcher, retro arcade, space strategy), and post each to UI Review so Brett can pick one. Reference: the Gizmo chat restyle from October. Brett's words: "The entirety of, of AmberX. Rewrite, rebuild the whole thing. Use its own style, its own design, its own color theme, its own layout. Just build that shit from scratch. Give me a whole shitload of fucking UI reviews to pick from, man." and "Make it look good, give it a really good, like a Windows game."

notes.text: Every concept must look and feel like a real, working desktop application, not a mockup or static screenshot: real navigation, working screens, real controls and states, using AmberX's actual features and data. Brett: "I love the design to look like a real application, dude."

PREVIEWS FIRST. Each of the 8 steps now only produces a preview (static mockup screens of what Patches / AmberX would closely look like in that style) and posts it to UI Review. Do NOT build any real app code. Stop after all 8 previews and wait for Brett to pick one in UI Review; only the picked concept gets fully built. Note: patches.amberxai.com (the Patches app) was deleted; the picked concept becomes its from-scratch rebuild. Brett: "before you go crazy building, I need some previews in the UI review. Okay, what it closely might look like."

ARCHITECTURE for the real build (after Brett picks a preview): compile Patches, AmberX, the Dev Console and axHub controls into ONE app with one look and one login. Front end: a game-launcher style home hub with a tile per module (AmberX, Console, Builds, UI Review, etc.) plus a sidebar to jump between them. Modular and stable: each module is its own service/container on the VPS with axHub as the gateway, so one module can crash, restart or be rebuilt without taking down the rest. Every module gets a health check and auto-restart; code for each module lives in its own folder on GitHub with nightly backups so nothing is lost again. MODELS: the orchestrator picks the model for every step; ignore the Opus set on the steps. Brett: "I want to do all those things but yeah the orchestrator is supposed to pick the model"

before.title: Universal voice + API control (everything controllable)
before.detail: Every setting, every screen and every button in the whole app (console, axHub, patches, AmberX, everything) must be fully controllable by the API and by voice. Everything is already an asset and a token, so build one control registry: each control gets a stable ID, type, allowed actions and a description; the API can list, find and act on any of them; voice maps spoken commands onto those API calls. Separate build so it can run in parallel with the others.

before.title: Slot-aware plan optimizer (pre-launch)
before.detail: Before the orchestrator launches a plan from the queue, it checks how many parallel sessions are enabled and how many slots are open, then optimizes/refactors the plan to use all available slots: build a dependency graph of the steps, group independent steps into parallel tracks (one per free slot), keep dependent steps in order, and give each track its own brief. Re-check slots at launch time; if slots change, re-balance.

steps.text: Read enabled parallel sessions and currently open slots at launch time
Late account binding: no account or session assigned in pending/queue; when the plan's turn comes up, count free slots on every Claude account and assign tracks across all accounts to fill every slot
Step dependency graph for a plan (which steps can run independently)
File ownership: each parallel track owns its own files; steps only run in parallel when their files don't overlap; lock shared files (configs) so sessions don't step on each other
Optimizer: split independent steps into N parallel tracks to fill free slots
Generate a separate brief per track; merge/progress markers per track
Rebalance when slots open or close mid-build + end-to-end test

Model-aware slots: when scanning accounts/slots, also read which models each account has available (Fable limit hit or not); Fable steps only go to accounts with Fable available; if no Fable anywhere, only Opus runs

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. Still open here: the check at split time, the AmberX conflict notice and the ledger backfill.

before.title: UI = API parity: builds, plans and orchestration screens
before.detail: Part of the "every UI is fully API-controllable" rule (ui-api@1; build ui-api-parity-rule, which did the Demonstration Designer and Book Builder and the CI check). 437 gaps across 13 UI area(s) today (framework/spec/ui-parity-baseline.json). Per area: `node framework/cli/ui-parity.mjs gaps <area>`, then map each view/dialog in its plugin.json `ui` block (open = deep link, state = read command or value:<key>, actions = commands / console actions / settings, uiOnly with why), add any op that is missing, and `ui-parity.mjs write-baseline` once it went down. Model of a full map: apps/console-web/plugins/glossary-index/plugin.json `ui`. Audit: _claude/builds/reports/ui-api-parity-rule/audit.md.

notes.text: Clash: orchestrator-full-api-control (pending) adds step hold/resume/kill to the Build orchestrator; build them together so its controls are mapped once.

origin.said:
Standing rule: anything with a UI must have API functions that can do everything the UI can (open, read state, every action, every setting). Voice control is the app's main selling point and rides on this.

1. Orchestrator: every brief it writes for a build that touches UI includes this requirement explicitly (brief template + brief writer). Keep it short.
2. CI check: every registered UI asset/control/plugin view maps to API operations covering its actions and settings; fail when missing; report gaps.
3. Audit: list every existing UI lacking full API coverage, starting with the glossary/index Demonstration Designer and Book Builder; fix those two here, add the rest as pending builds.
4. Deep link per plugin view (URL that opens it) so agents can open any UI on the phone.

origin.said: AmberX notification panel (Brett): A real notification panel inside the AmberX phone app that receives every kind of notification and status from the console, orchestrator, axHub and builds. 1. Typed notifications: build started/done/failed, approvals and veto holds (with Deny / Run now), account status (checks starting/done, expired, limit, no credits), UI Review items, alerts, info. Extensible type registry. 2. Panel: list grouped by type/source, filters, unread counts, search, mark read, clear, pin; tap opens the related screen; action buttons per type. 3. Live status area: current account statuses, running builds, queue. 4. Also delivered as Android push notifications with actions; panel keeps history. 5. One send API every plugin uses (console, orchestrator, axHub); reuse existing notifications/alert hub code (notifications-control-panel groups/triggers/actions) where it exists. Rules: Full API + voice + MCP/CLI control; settings in categorized collapsible sections (per-type on/off, sound, priority); 3 UI options to UI Review; phone screenshots; tests; report, STATUS, THREADS.
origin.brief: Launched directly from voice (no record); text is the launch brief.

steps.text: Server core: kinds registry (notify-panel-types@1), classify alerts, send API → alert hub, pins/read/clear, live status (accounts, running builds, queue); tests
Routes + plugin-commands (MCP/CLI), capability axf.notify-panel@1 for senders, voice phrases, settings sections (per-type on/off, sound, priority via notify-control)
Panel view (console + AmberX): grouped list, filters, unread counts, search, mark read, clear, pin, per-kind actions, approvals with Deny / Run now, live status area
AmberX Android push: console alert notifications carry action buttons (open / panel) and the tap opens the panel item
UI Review (3 options as assets, phone shots), report, STATUS, THREADS, PR to the merge queue

before.title: Slot watchdog crew member (Slot Warden)
before.detail: Plain-code watchdog (zero tokens) on the headless build slots and queue: every ~30 s checks each running slot against reality (tmux alive, claude pid alive, log advancing); dead / finished / hung -> release slot, mark build failed with reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator, notify Brett (type slot). Live status + intervention log in console and AmberX. Root fix: claude-headless.sh always releases its slot when Claude exits. Duplicate guard on launch and in the watchdog (reuses orchestrator-dup-check). Crew member Slot Warden on the roster.

origin.said:
Assign a crew member (agent profile in the roster, e.g. a 'Slot Warden') whose only job is watching the headless build slots and queue, all the time, in plain code (zero tokens).

1. Every ~30 s: check each running slot in framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs against reality (tmux session alive, claude -p pid alive, log advancing). Today 3 builds died in 1-3 s on bad logins but kept all 3 slots, freezing the queue.
2. Dead / finished / hung (no log progress past a threshold) -> release the slot, mark the build failed with the reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator so it can relaunch/fail over (account-health-failover build), and notify Brett's phone (AmberX notification panel, type 'slot').
3. Report: a live slot/queue status the console and AmberX show; a log of every intervention.
4. Also fix the root: claude-headless.sh must always finish/release its slot when Claude exits, even on instant auth failure.

Duplicate guard (Brett): The watchdog and the launcher refuse or stop duplicate builds: same brief/goal running twice (e.g. memory-manager-r2 and -r3 both ran). On launch, compare against running + queued builds (name stem, brief source, build id); keep the furthest-along one, stop/dequeue the other, tell the orchestrator and notify Brett. Reuse the unlanded orchestrator-dup-check branch.

before.title: Agent profile schema: skills + personas, with a big template library
before.detail: Contract work (Fable). New asset schemas for crew agents: agent-skill@1 (name, domain, what it does, tools allowed, files/areas it owns, rules, checks it runs, model preference, cost cap, examples) and agent-persona@1 (name, nickname, voice/tone, job title, avatar, how it reports, strengths, limits), plus agent-profile@1 that combines one persona with several skills. Validators, fixtures, CI check. Ship a large library of boilerplate templates: skills (React UI, Kotlin/Compose, Python server, plugin manifests, themes/skins, tests, docs, merge-fixer, CI fixer, slot watchdog, account health, notifications, voice/API wiring, security review, UI Review designer, demo/pitch writer, data/Postgres, deploy/Coolify, refactor, perf) and personas (lander, reviewer, builder, watchdog, reporter, etc.). Template picker + 'new from template' in the Crew plugin; migrate the existing roster (Earl, Rhonda, Sully, Lenny, Gina, Paulie, Joey, Vinnie) onto it. Orchestrator reads skills when assigning steps. Every UI gets full API + voice + MCP/CLI control. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

before.title: Headless loop guards: stop endless loops and searches
before.detail: Guards on every headless session the orchestrator launches (claude-headless.sh + agent-slots + the running-builds watchdog's afterTick hook in pipeline.mjs): 1) Hard caps per session: --max-turns, wall time and cost cap derived from the step estimates (e.g. 2x estimate), settings with defaults. 2) Step progress timer: no step tick within 1.5x the step's estimate -> warn note, at 2x -> stop the session, build back to pending with the reason. 3) Loop detector reading the live log: the same command/tool call (or near-identical grep/find/sed) repeated N times, or M searches in a row with no edit/commit -> stop and note. 4) Search budget per step (e.g. 15 greps/finds) written into the brief and enforced by the detector. 5) Every stop: build note with the reason and last log lines, AmberX notification (normal notification, not an alarm), slot released, no auto-relaunch of a looped step until Brett says. 6) Brief line: 'If you can't find something in 3 searches, stop and leave a note.' Settings in orchestrator settings (categorized sections), full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests with fake logs: repeated command, search spree, no tick, cost cap.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "I need a way to manage the safeguards." Add a Safeguards panel (orchestrator settings, its own section, also reachable from the build's row): turn each guard on/off; edit turns cap, time cap (x estimate), cost cap, no-tick warn/stop multipliers, repeat-command count, search budget; per-build and per-queue overrides; a live view of each running session against its limits (turns, time, cost, searches used); a log of every guard stop with the reason, last log lines and buttons: Relaunch, Raise limit and relaunch, Send back to pending. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and a deep link. Stock controls, 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett on managing the safeguards: "I don't want the file itself to be editable. I want it to be view. You can view the file with steps. Make it an MD file with bullet points for the rules. And create a sortable, collapsible tree with a whole shitload of different rules, of snippets. When you click it, it will pop a dialogue to let you add the custom fields that it requires for the snippet and it will insert it." Build: 1) The safeguards live as a Markdown rules file (one bullet per rule, grouped by heading), shown READ-ONLY in the panel (rendered view with the steps it applies to); no free-text editing. 2) A snippet library: a sortable, searchable, collapsible tree (category > sub-category > snippet) with a large set of ready rule snippets (turn caps, time/cost caps, no-tick timeouts, repeat-command and search-spree limits, file/folder fences, no sub-agents, model limits, test-before-commit, stop-and-note rules, etc.). 3) Clicking a snippet opens a dialog with the fields it needs (number, duration, $, path, model, scope: global/queue/build/step) with validation and a preview line; Insert adds the bullet to the rules file. 4) Each inserted rule can be toggled, moved, or removed from the panel (structured actions, still no raw edit); every change is versioned with history and undo. 5) The orchestrator and the loop detector read their limits from this file; the brief gets the bullets that apply to the step. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control; stock controls; 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett: "the dialogue that needs custom parameters for the rules, any that are like file names or specific things already have a list to choose from for the custom parameters." In the snippet fields dialog, every field whose values already exist is a pick list (searchable dropdown or tree picker), not free text: file and folder paths (from the repo tree / plugin registry), plugins, apps, builds, queues, steps, Claude accounts, API accounts, models, agents/crew, tools, commands, settings keys. Multi-select where a rule takes several. Free text only for true free values (numbers, durations, $ amounts) and those get validated inputs with units.

Brett: "There has to be filters too, where you put in for the list of certain types of parameters. There's got to be filters." Every pick list in the snippet dialog has filters fitting its type, plus search: files/folders by app, plugin, folder, file type/extension, changed recently, owned by a build; plugins by app, category, enabled; builds by status, queue, model, category, date; queues by account type; steps by build and state; accounts by role, model available, health; models by tier; agents by role/skill; tools by service; settings keys by plugin/section. Filters combine, show counts, can be cleared, and remember the last used per field.

Brett: "list of features. Stack. And the list of predefined search terms based on what the rule is." 1) Filters stack (combine) and include a 'feature' filter: pick from the Shipped features list / plugin feature catalog to narrow files, builds and steps to one feature. 2) Each snippet carries predefined search terms and preset filter stacks that fit that rule (e.g. a file-fence rule offers 'server routes', 'web views', 'plugin.json', 'tests', 'schemas'; a model rule offers 'Fable-only steps', 'UI steps'), shown as quick chips in the pick list; tap one to apply. Brett can save his own presets per snippet.

Brett: "as you type in the field, it automatically drops down the list of all the ones that match. Whatever you type. In real time. Letter per letter." Every parameter field is a type-ahead combobox: the match list drops down on the first letter and updates on every keystroke (fuzzy match, matched letters highlighted, within the active filters), keyboard up/down/enter and tap to pick. Fast on large lists (indexed/virtualized, no lag).

Brett: "And they pop up in a categorized tree." The live type-ahead drop-down shows its matches as a categorized collapsible tree (e.g. app > plugin > folder > file; queue > build > step; account type > account), branches with matches auto-expand, counts per branch, empty branches hidden; picking a branch can select all under it where the rule allows several.

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. before.title: UI Roller: roll a random style on any UI element
before.detail: New UI Roller plugin (console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web; every app built on the framework). 1) Context menu on EVERY UI element (dialogs, windows, panels, bars, buttons, inputs, menus, text, widgets; all registry assets): 'Roll style' and, when the element has a roll, 'Reset element'. 2) 'Roll style' opens a dialog: checkboxes for what to roll (colours, typography, spacing/density, size, radius/shape, borders, shadows, motion, icons), optional scope (this element / all of its type / its plugin), live preview, Re-roll, Apply. Rolls stay within valid token ranges and keep contrast readable. Apply saves the result as asset token overrides (local-first, like other overrides). 3) Main Settings > Rolled assets page: lists every app and plugin with its rolled assets (tree, counts, filters, search); each shows a live preview of the asset and its roll; actions: Reset (one), Reset selected (multi-select), Reset all. Undo/history per roll. 4) Applying a skin, design pack or theme clears EVERY rolled asset: covered ones take the new look, all others go back to their defaults. 5) Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep links for roll, reset, reset selected/all and the page. Stock framework controls; 3 layout options to UI Review; tests (roll writes tokens, reset restores, theme apply clears all rolls); report.

before.title: Skins are a complete rework: look + layout + behavior, and professional skins
before.detail: After skins-finish lands (skin@1 + skin-coverage@1 for every asset type). Today a skin covers look only; layout and behavior live in design packs. Change: a skin is the complete rework of an app. Extend skin@1 (contract, Fable) to carry everything a design pack does: look (colors, grid and hover/selection colors, typography sizes, spacing/density, radius, borders, shadows, icons, motion), layout (nav placement, app menu, toolbars, banners, panel arrangement, grid density) and behavior (how menus open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions, overflow rules) for every registry asset type: nav menu, app menu, context menu, grids, dialogs, windows, bars, widgets, text. Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. before.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
before.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 8 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: Why do you have to guess its ID? Why can't you get it? ... Yeah, of course.

steps.text: Design the reservation model in the orchestrator's ID registry. Add a `reserved` state with reservedAt, origin call, kind (build|plan) and holdId. Add a per-ID ordered queue of pending ops (note, sub prompt, status), each with a seq and a payload. Store it in _claude/builds/store.json and add a migration that leaves existing entries untouched. Write the registry API in pipeline-core.mjs: reserveId(title, kind) checks for collisions against live builds, plans, shipped and existing reservations; commitReservation(id) turns a reservation into a real build; dropReservation(id) removes it and its queue.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for the build ID registry, which every port's contract depends on

steps.text: Change the veto-hold contract so the ID is reserved before the hold starts. Held results carry reservedId, holdId and secondsLeft. On approve or timeout, commitReservation runs and then the queued ops are replayed in seq order. On deny, dropReservation runs. Write down the contract for every caller: pending_change add, control_add on planner.builds/plans, plan_park, plan_add.
steps.why: Cross-port contract change to the held-result shape that all callers rely on

steps.text: Wire pending_change add and control_add (planner.builds and planner.plans) through reserveId so the held result returns reservedId right away. Approve and deny on the hold call commit or drop the reservation.
Wire plan_park and plan_add the same way: reserve the ID before the hold, return reservedId in the held result, and commit or drop when the hold resolves.

Queue notes, sub prompts and status calls that target a reserved ID. The note, sub prompt and status handlers check whether the ID is reserved and, if so, add the op to the queue instead of failing. The queued result says queued:true with its seq. Replay applies the ops in order after the add runs.
Show the reserved ID and the queued op count on the veto countdown card in the console Build manager. Add a 'copy ID' action. Deep link: console_show target build-orchestrator/hold/<reservedId>.

API part for the reservation and countdown UI. REST: GET /api/builds/reservations and GET /api/builds/reservations/<id> read the state (status, secondsLeft, queued ops); POST approve and POST deny act on the hold. MCP: console actions builds.reservation.get, builds.reservation.approve and builds.reservation.deny, plus control@1 for planner items. CLI: axf builds reservation get|approve|deny <id>. AmberX voice intents for the same three actions. All four surfaces call the same handlers.

Tests, report and PR. Write tests for: add returns the ID while held; a note on the reserved ID lands after the add runs; deny drops the reservation and its queued note; no ID collision when two adds with the same title arrive together; plan_park and plan_add return reservedId; REST, MCP and CLI give the same results. Write _claude/builds/reports/reserve-build-ids-at-once-add-returns-the-id-wit.md. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, stating how the reservation and countdown are reached through the deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Permissions control panel: every axHub tool's policy in one place
before.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. Brett changes a policy with a dropdown; bulk change per service or by filter (destructive, writes, reads). Tree grouped by service > category, search, filters, live type-ahead. Every change logged with history and undo. Claude sessions and builds can read policies but never change them (owner-only, enforced on the hub, not just the UI). First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: I need a control panel for all those settings, those permission settings.

steps.text: Design the axHub policy store schema and migration. One record per tool (service, tool id, category tags destructive/writes/reads, mode allow|veto|confirm|deny, countdown seconds, allowed callers brett-session|claude-session|headless-build|agent, passes). Add an append-only change-history table with actor, before/after and undo link. Write a migration that imports today's scattered veto/confirm/pass settings into the store without changing any effective policy.
steps.why: Schema plus migration design for the hub's central policy store

steps.text: Define the cross-port policy contract axhub-policy@1. It covers REST shapes (tree, search, filter, get, set, bulk set, history, undo), MCP tool names, control@1 ops, the CLI verbs, the live change event stream, and owner-only write semantics with error codes. Every surface (console API, MCP, CLI, AmberX voice) maps 1:1 to it.
steps.why: Cross-port contract shared by hub, console, MCP, CLI and voice

steps.text: Build the tool registry inventory. Enumerate every connected service and tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx, ...) from the hub's connection manifests. Classify each tool into a category and destructive/writes/reads, and seed missing tools with a safe default (confirm). Re-sync when a service connects or disconnects.

Enforce policies on the hub, not in the UI. The tool-call gate resolves caller identity (Brett session, Claude session, headless build, agent) and applies allow/veto countdown/confirm/deny plus the caller list and passes. Policy writes are owner-only: any non-owner caller gets 403 with a clear message. Reads stay open to all authenticated callers.

Add the history and undo service. Every single or bulk change is written as one history entry, with a bulk change grouped under one id. Undo restores the before-state, is itself logged, and is also owner-only. Each change emits a live event for the panel.

Add the REST routes: GET /policies (tree grouped by service > category, with q= type-ahead search and filters by mode/category/caller), GET /policies/:tool, PUT /policies/:tool, POST /policies/bulk (by service or by filter), GET /policies/history, POST /policies/history/:id/undo. Write routes go through owner-only enforcement. Proxy the routes through the console API.

Expose the same operations through MCP and the CLI. Add MCP console actions (policy.list/get/set/bulk/history/undo), control@1 ops for policy items, and CLI `axf policy list|get|set|bulk|history|undo` with the same filters. Writes from Claude sessions and builds are rejected by the hub.

Add AmberX voice intents for Brett. Read intents: 'what's the policy for vps.run', 'which tools are deny'. Write intents: 'set github writes to confirm', 'undo last permission change', 'open permissions'. Writes need the owner voice session and are spoken back before they apply.

Build the shared Permissions panel core in console/axhub-web. It includes the data hook on GET /policies with live events, the policy dropdown per tool, countdown and caller editors, pass list, bulk change bar (per service or current filter), live type-ahead search, filter chips (destructive/writes/reads, mode, caller), and a history drawer with undo. Register deep link console_show/console_open target 'permissions' (with optional tool= / service= / filter=). Make the panel state readable via the console state API.

Build layout option A: a collapsible tree (service > category > tool) with an inline dropdown per row and a sticky bulk bar. It reuses the core and adds no new actions. The deep link 'permissions?layout=a' and the state read come from the core.

Build layout option B (dense filterable table with column sort and multi-select) and layout option C (service cards with a per-service default and expandable tool lists). Both reuse the core. Add deep links 'permissions?layout=b|c'.
Submit the 3 layouts to UI Review with screenshots and deep links. Add a setting for the chosen layout, readable and settable through REST, MCP, CLI (`axf policy layout`) and voice.

Make the first change as owner through the API: set vps.build_start to deny for every caller except the orchestrator's build-launch identity (via a pass). Check that a Claude session and a headless build are refused and that the orchestrator still launches builds. Record the change in policy history.

Write tests covering: migration keeps effective policies unchanged; enforcement for every mode and caller; owner-only writes rejected for Claude sessions, builds and agents on REST, MCP, CLI and voice; bulk by service and by filter; history and undo; registry sync; type-ahead search and filters; deep link and state read for each layout.

Run the full test suites and fix any failures. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/permissions-control-panel-every-axhub-tool-s-pol.md (what was built, the vps.build_start change, how each UI part is reached via deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI and voice). Add the THREADS row and open the PR, with the same API access table in the PR description.
