before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: results pop up in a scrolling window. As Brett types in Search everything (or the recorder page), matching transcript snippets pop up live in a scrolling results window: each hit shows the session (date, title), timestamp and a few lines around the match with the words highlighted; infinite scroll, grouped by session, newest first with a sort switch. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

Brett: "With the keywords in focus." In the scrolling results window each snippet is centered on the matched keywords, highlighted. Opening a hit scrolls the transcript so the keyword is centered on screen, highlighted and focused, with next/previous match buttons inside that session.

Brett: "there's a column on the left with all the hits. All the sessions that match: the session name and the type of thing we were talking about." Results window layout: left column lists every session with hits (session name, date, hit count, and a topic tag for what it was about, e.g. builds, skins, approvals, AmberX); tapping one shows its hits on the right, keywords centered and highlighted. Topic tags: from the linked Claude session's title and the builds it touched (plain code, zero tokens); optionally a cheap one-time tag per session after transcription, off by default.

Brett: "I want a RAG database made of all the transcripts." Build a RAG store over every transcript: chunk each transcript (with session, date, timestamps, speaker, topic tags), embed the chunks with a local embedding model on the VPS (no Claude tokens), store them in Postgres with pgvector (reuse the postgres-console container plan if it exists, else its own table), and index every new transcript automatically after transcription. Two ways in: 1) semantic search (meaning, not just exact words) in the same results window, mixed with the keyword hits; 2) 'Ask' (API/MCP/voice): Claude or Gizmo retrieve the top chunks and answer with the sessions and timestamps as sources, each linking to that moment. Share the store with the Agent Manager's RAG knowledge (agent-profile build) so employees can use it. Settings: on/off, re-index, what gets indexed. Tests: retrieval returns the right session for a paraphrased question.
Split by rules (Claude: claude not available: spawnSync claude ETIMEDOUT): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 11 steps (1 Fable).

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

steps.text: Design the transcript index: a schema for per-session metadata (id, date, length, title, linked Claude session id) and timestamped segments that the hub transcripts map onto, plus a migration that backfills the index from transcripts already saved on the hub. Document the contract that the API commands return (session, segment, match with context and deep link).
steps.why: Schema + migration design and a cross-port contract that MCP, REST, CLI and voice all share

steps.text: Build a read-only transcript reader over the hub store. It lists sessions that have transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title) with paging and date filters, and reads one transcript either whole or for a start/end time range, with a timestamp on every segment.

Build search across all transcripts. It supports words, exact phrase, date range and fuzzy matching (typo-tolerant), and returns the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context and a deep link. Add the find-session ranking, which scores each session by its matches (count, phrase proximity, recency) for 'the session where we talked about X'.

Enforce the recorder's settings in the reader and search: recording or transcription off, retention window, sessions excluded or marked private, and the hub read scope. Every path stays read-only with no writes or deletes, and blocked results are returned as clear errors.

Declare the transcript commands in output-recorder plugin.json under plugin-commands@1: transcripts.list, transcripts.read, transcripts.search, transcripts.find_session and recorder.page_state. Each gets a parameter schema and is wired to its handler, so axHub MCP, console REST, CLI and voice pick them up.

Recorder page deep link (UI change, with its API part in this same step). The page opens at ?session=<id>&t=<sec>&play=1, scrolls the transcript to that moment, seeks the audio and plays it. Register it as a console_show/console_open target. The page state (open session, position, playing) is readable through recorder.page_state, and the open, seek and play actions are callable without the UI over REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Make sure the commands are exposed the same way on REST (console API routes) and the CLI (transcripts list/read/search/find-session with --from/--to/--fuzzy/--json). Help text and output include the deep link.

Expose the commands through axHub MCP for Claude chat and voice sessions and Gizmo. Add voice intents for 'which session did we talk about X', 'read what was said at …' and 'open that session'. The spoken answer gives the session title, date and timestamp, and offers to open the deep link.

Unit tests: reader time ranges and timestamps, phrase, word and fuzzy search, date filter, context lines, find_session ranking order, policy enforcement (disabled, retention, private, read-only), and the index backfill migration.

Parity and integration tests: the same query through REST, MCP, CLI and voice gives the same result. The deep link opens the recorder page at the timestamp and plays the audio, and recorder.page_state reflects it.

Run the full test suite and fix any failures. Write the report, add the THREADS row and open the PR. The PR describes how each feature is reached: deep link, state read, actions and settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Split builds pages (Build Manager = Pending + Complete; Orchestrator = Queued + Active) with one clean shared table design
before.detail:
Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded).

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator: account that actually built it, model, cost, PR, land status). Build orchestrator owns only Queued and Active (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending); finished builds go back to Build Manager Complete. Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: one shared framework build-table asset used by all four tabs so they look the same. Each build is one clean compact line (title, priority, status badge, steps done/total, account, model) that expands; inside the expanded row, collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps with state, runs/sessions, cost, files/PR, Brett's words, log tail). Per-tab columns differ only where needed: Active shows a live elapsed timer, steps complete with a progress bar, current step, account actually running it; Queued shows position and why it's waiting; Complete shows duration, cost, who built it. Clean, minimal, theme tokens only, phone and desktop. Screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 11 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: Clean those tables up. One line that's expandable, with collapsible grids or sections inside the expanded row. All the tables need to look the same. The active ones need to show the timer, how long they've been going, how many steps are complete. Build manager will have pending and complete. Orchestrator will have active and queued.

steps.text: Define the build lifecycle contract between Build Manager and the orchestrator. Pending → Send → Queued. Queued → cancel/return → Pending. Queued → Active. Active → finished → Build Manager Complete. The completion record carries the account that actually built it, model, cost, PR, land status, start/end/duration and steps done/total. Add a store schema version bump plus a migration that moves existing finished, queued and active records into the new buckets. Mark one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove as superseded by this build.
steps.why: Schema + migration design and the cross-port handoff contract between two apps

Include an expand/collapse state API, theme tokens only, and a responsive phone/desktop layout.

Add the Build Manager Complete tab on the shared build-table. It shows finished builds sent back by the orchestrator: account that built it, model, cost, PR link, land status and duration. Expanded sections show steps, runs, cost, files/PR, Brett's words and log tail.

Expose all of this through REST routes, MCP console actions/plugin commands, the CLI subcommands and AmberX voice intents, with the same behavior on all four.

Rebuild the orchestrator page with only Queued and Active tabs on the shared build-table. Queued shows position and why it's waiting, with route, assign account, hold, and cancel/return to Pending. Active shows the live elapsed timer, steps-complete progress bar, current step and the account actually running it. When a build finishes it is posted to Build Manager Complete through the handoff contract.

Give the orchestrator full API control for Queued and Active. Deep links: orchestrator/queued, orchestrator/active and orchestrator/build/<id>. Expose all of this through REST, MCP (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 where tokens are involved), the CLI and AmberX voice, with the same behavior on all four.

Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen. Old routes and deep links (build-queue, builds, built) redirect to the matching new tab in the REST, MCP, CLI and voice aliases. Delete dead CSS and JS.
Update the docs for the page split, the shared build-table asset and the API reach. Take phone and desktop screenshots of all four tabs, collapsed and expanded, and post them to UI Review.

Tests cover the build-table render, expand and sections, the store migration, the handoff Pending→Queued→Active→Complete and return-to-Pending, redirects, and REST/MCP/CLI/voice parity for every action. Run the suite. Write the report to _claude/builds/reports/split-builds-pages-build-manager-pending-complet-2.md and add a THREADS row. Open the PR, stating how each UI feature is reached through the deep link, state read, actions and settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Standing rule in every brief: fix problems yourself, log and notify, never stop to ask
before.detail: Add to the orchestrator's brief rules (every build it splits and briefs), the headless session rules, agent profiles and the shared CLAUDE rules every Claude session reads: when something blocks the work, try every fix within your permissions (axHub tools, console, VPS check/run, Coolify, hosting, or hand off to an agent with the right permissions) and keep going; don't stop to ask Brett. Log each attempt and send him an FYI notification through AmberX (trying X / X failed / trying Y / fixed) using the fix-log tool; informational, never a permission request. Existing approval gates on VPS writes stay as they are.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 8 steps (0 Fable).

origin.said: From now on, you do whatever in your ability to fix any problem. I don't want to be bothered... just notify me of doing it, not for permission or veto. ... Every single build, put that in the brief... put it where you need to so that anything that's doing anything will be able to follow those rules.

steps.text: Write the canonical standing rule in _claude/shared/rules/fix-it-yourself.md. When something blocks the work, try every fix within your permissions: axHub tools, console, VPS check/run, Coolify, hosting, or hand off to an agent that has the right permissions. Keep going and never stop to ask Brett. Log each attempt with the fix-log tool, which sends Brett an FYI through AmberX (trying X / X failed / trying Y / fixed). The FYI is informational, never a permission request or veto. Existing approval gates on VPS writes stay as they are. Include Brett's verbatim quote and a short how-to for the fix-log tool. Link the rule from _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md so it sits in the always-read set.

Wire the rule into the shared CLAUDE rules every Claude session reads. Add a short pointer section to the repo CLAUDE.md and the shared CLAUDE instructions synced by claude-sync. Make sure the claude-sync manifest ships fix-it-yourself.md to every project.

Orchestrator brief rules: add the standing rule as a fixed block in the brief every build gets. Put it in BRIEF-TEMPLATE.md and in the orchestrator's brief builder, which always injects it no matter what the build's details say. Also add a line to the splitter prompt saying the rule applies to every step.

Headless session rules: add the rule to the system prompt / --append-system-prompt the orchestrator passes to every headless Claude Code step and probe. Cover both the Fable and Opus paths, and the resume/retry path.

Agent profiles: add the rule, or a reference to it, to every agent profile and agent definition. This covers _claude/builds/profiles/* (all, breakroom, others) and .claude/agents/*. New profiles created from the template inherit it.

Fix-log tool: check that it records each attempt (trying / failed / fixed, with what was tried) and sends the AmberX notification as an FYI only, with no approve/veto buttons and no waiting for a reply. It must be callable the same way from the CLI, MCP tool, console REST route and AmberX voice, so headless sessions can use it. Fill any gaps and add the reach-paths to the tool's README.

Add one sentence in fix-it-yourself.md and in the VPS tool docs saying the gate still applies: a gated write goes through the existing approval and is logged as an attempt, not bypassed.

Run the suites and write _claude/builds/reports/standing-rule-in-every-brief-fix-problems-yourse.md. Add a THREADS.md row. Open a PR that states this build adds no UI and lists how the fix-log tool is reached (CLI / MCP / REST / voice).

Screenshots go to UI Review grouped by screen.

before.detail: Follows the skins-as-section-packages build; upgrade that and reuse existing pieces (the IDE layout and tab groups from walkthrough-player-ide-layout-setting-collapsibl, the Demonstration designer, and UI asset designer). 1) PREVIEW EVERYWHERE: every list and grid that shows skin chunks or assets gets a preview action (hover thumbnail plus a full preview pane). 2) INTERACTIVE DEMO: if a chunk can be demoed (behaviour, layouts, components), Demo opens a live sandbox where you can actually use it. Split by Claude into 16 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: When you're looking at these lists and any of the grids of these chunks, you can preview one, or open a demo of it if it can be demoed, an interactive demonstration where you can actually use it, or at the very least a preview of what the chunk looks like. And the ability to view them side by side, multiple containers with tab groups, mix and match elements in multiple floating containers to compare side by side. An IDE-style thing with a bunch of floating tab groups with different types of assets in them, with the info on the chunk, and you can drag them to each other and build new things side by side. Each tab can be split with a preview and an editor so you can see changes in real time.

steps.text: Design the chunk preview and demo contract and the studio layout schema. Chunk manifest fields: demo capability (interactive kind: behaviour, layout or component; sandbox entry; rendered-preview fallback) and a thumbnail spec. Studio layout document: tab groups (docked or floating, position and size), tabs (asset ref, type, split state), compare containers, and named saved layouts. Add a migration that upgrades the existing IDE layout settings from walkthrough-player-ide-layout and the skin section-package manifests from skins-as-section-packages.
steps.why: Schema and migration design shared by the skins, demo and studio ports

steps.text: Extend the framework IDE layout engine taken from walkthrough-player-ide-layout. Tab groups become dockable or floating. Groups hold tabs of any asset type through a tab-type registry. Tabs can be dragged between groups and between docked and floating groups. Groups can be nested into compare containers. All of this is driven by the new layout document.
steps.why: Changes how the IDE-layout GUI works for every app that uses it

steps.text: Add the split-tab primitive and the live-update channel. Any tab can split into an editor pane and a preview pane. Edits flow to the preview in real time over a debounced change stream with the same contract for every asset type. Bad edits show an error overlay in the preview and keep the last good render.
steps.why: Engine internals and a cross-port editor/preview contract

steps.text: Add server-side preview rendering for skin chunks and UI assets: a cached thumbnail renderer and a full-preview render endpoint. Thumbnails are invalidated when a chunk changes. Reuse the UI asset designer renderer.

Add a preview action to every list and grid that shows skin chunks or assets: the skins section-package lists, pack grids, the UI asset designer library and the demonstration designer pickers. Hovering shows a thumbnail and Preview opens a full preview pane.

Add full API control for preview. Deep link console_open target skins/preview/<chunk>. Readable preview state. Actions preview.open, preview.close and preview.thumbnail. All of it reachable the same way through REST routes, MCP console actions and plugin commands, the CLI and AmberX voice intents.

Add the interactive demo. Demo opens a live sandbox for demoable chunks (behaviour, layouts, components) by reusing the Demonstration designer sandbox, so you can actually use the chunk. Chunks that cannot be demoed fall back to a rendered preview. The Demo action is added next to Preview in every list and grid.

Add full API control for demo. Deep link console_open skins/demo/<chunk>. Readable sandbox state (running, mode interactive or rendered). Actions demo.open, demo.reset and demo.close. All of it reachable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Add the compare view. Open any number of chunks side by side in containers that can be docked or floating. Containers can mix asset types, and each container is a tab group from the extended layout engine.

Add the IDE studio as an optional view, off by default and switched on with a setting, not forced. It shows floating and dockable tab groups holding any asset types, plus a chunk info panel with name, category, source skin, tags and used-by. Used-by comes from a reverse-reference index built on the server.

Add drag-to-compose in the studio. Dropping a chunk onto another chunk, or into a pack template, creates a new skin or asset draft through the UI asset designer and the skins section-package builder, then opens the draft in a new tab.

Wire split tabs into the studio and compare views for every asset tab type. Each type gets an editor and a live preview that updates in real time over the live-preview channel, with a split toggle on every tab.

Add saving and restoring of layouts. Named studio and compare layouts can be saved, listed, restored, renamed and deleted. They are stored per profile and the last-used layout is restored automatically.

Add full API control for compare, the studio, split tabs, compose and layouts. Deep links: console_open skins/studio, skins/compare?chunks=… and skins/studio?layout=…. Readable state: groups, tabs, split state, info panel. Actions: open, close and move tabs; float and dock groups; split and unsplit; compose; layout save, restore and delete; the studio-view setting. All of it the same through REST, MCP (console actions and plugin commands, control@1 for tokens), the CLI and voice.
Capture desktop and phone screenshots of the list previews, demo sandbox, rendered fallback, compare, studio, info panel, split tab and layouts, and send them to UI Review grouped by screen.

Add tests for the schema migration, the layout engine (drag, float, dock), split live updates, the preview, demo, compose and layout routes, and REST/MCP/CLI/voice parity. Then write the report at _claude/builds/reports/skin-chunk-previews-interactive-demos-and-an-ide.md, add the THREADS row, and open the PR. The PR lists how each UI feature is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Landing tool takes long build names, and auto-fixes and retries failed lands
before.detail: vps.build_land, build_start, build_stop and build_clean reject names over 40 characters (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$), but the orchestrator makes build IDs up to about 50 characters (e.g. demo-designer-finish-phase-2-s2-s3-resuming-from, skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element). 1) In the axHub vps service, raise the name limit to match the orchestrator's longest IDs (at least 80), keeping the same safe character set. 2) If the orchestrator ever makes an ID the tools can't take, it shortens it consistently (folder, branch, tmux) instead of failing. 3) When build_land fails for any fixable reason (stray files, stale locks, name format), it fixes it and retries automatically, logging to the fix log. Real code clashes go to a conflict-fix build automatically. 4) Tests with long names. Repos: axHub (vps service config) and AmberX-AXF (orchestrator).

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 9 steps (1 Fable).

origin.said: Why, when it has a problem, when it gets rejected, aren't you just fixing it right away? I keep telling you over and over.

steps.text: Define the shared build-name contract used by both repos. Allowed names match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}$ (80 characters). Define one deterministic shortener: trim at a hyphen boundary, then append -<6-char hash of the full ID>, so the same long ID always maps to the same short name. The folder, branch and tmux session all use the short name. The orchestrator records long→short in its build record. Write the contract doc and the reference shortener module with its constants (max length, charset, hash length).
steps.why: Cross-port contract between the axHub vps service and the AmberX-AXF orchestrator

steps.text: axHub vps service: replace the hard-coded ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ in build_land, build_start, build_stop and build_clean with one shared constant from service config allowing up to 80 characters, with the same safe character set. Error messages state the limit and the offending length.

Orchestrator: route every place that makes a build ID, worktree folder, branch name or tmux session through build-name.mjs. When an ID exceeds the tools' limit, shorten it consistently instead of failing. Store long_id and short_id in the build record and journal. Lookups accept either form.
files: AmberX-AXF: apps/orchestrator/ (ID creation, worktree, branch, tmux spawn)

steps.text: Orchestrator: build_land failure classifier. Parse build_land errors into categories: stray_files (untracked or tmp files such as *.json.tmp-*), stale_lock (index.lock or a stale land lock with a dead PID), name_format (rejected name), code_conflict (real merge conflict) and unknown. Unit-testable pure function with fixtures from real failure output.

Orchestrator: auto-fix and retry loop around build_land. For each fixable category, apply the fixer: remove or commit stray tmp files after looking at them, clear stale locks only if the owning PID is dead, re-derive the short name for format rejects. Then retry, up to 3 attempts. Each attempt, fix and outcome is appended to the fix log. Land state (attempt, last error, fix applied) is readable through the existing console build API, MCP, CLI and voice status read.
files: AmberX-AXF: apps/console-web/ build status route/MCP/CLI land-state fields

steps.text: Orchestrator: on code_conflict, or when retries are used up on an unknown error, automatically queue a conflict-fix build. The queued build links to the parent build, the conflicting files and the failed land log. The parent build is marked waiting-on-fix in place of failed. Log it to the fix log.

axHub tests: build_land, build_start, build_stop and build_clean accept the 50 to 64 character real IDs (demo-designer-finish-phase-2-s2-s3-resuming-from, skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element) and an exactly-80-character name. They reject 81 characters, uppercase, a leading hyphen, slashes and dots.

AmberX-AXF tests: the shortener is deterministic, stays within the limit, keeps the folder, branch and tmux names identical, and has no collisions across the existing shipped build IDs. The classifier fixtures pass. The auto-fix loop recovers from stray files, stale locks and name format errors and logs to the fix log. A code conflict queues a conflict-fix build. A full long-name start, land and clean path is checked end to end against a mock vps.

Run the full test suites in both repos. Write the report: what changed, the name contract, each auto-fix category, the API reach of land state (REST, MCP, CLI, voice) and the test results with before and after. Add the THREADS row. Open PRs in axHub and AmberX-AXF, cross-linked, axHub merged first.

before.title: Auto-land every build the moment it finishes, redeploy the console on every land, and backfill the 134 unlanded
before.detail: Plain code in the orchestrator dispatcher, no AI. 1) The moment a build's session finishes with its steps ticked and tests green, the orchestrator lands it straight away: clean sync files and stray logs, clear stale locks, merge origin/main, rerun the build's own tests, push to main. No waiting on a person or a later session. 2) UPDATE THE CONSOLE ON EVERY LAND: right after each push to main, trigger the console redeploy immediately (the same path as install-console.sh's auto-update, run now, not on the 5-minute timer), and rebuild any other app the change touched (AmberX web, axHub web, Molly and so on). Wait for it to come up healthy, then refresh open consoles. If the deploy fails, roll back to the last good image and queue a fix. 3) UI Review never blocks landing: screenshots and picks can follow after landing, and changes come as follow-up builds. 4) If main moved and tests fail after the merge, or there's a code clash, the orchestrator immediately queues a conflict-fix run on the same branch (top priority, any working account) and lands when green. It retries until it's on main. 5) Land in finish order, one at a time (a merge lock), so each lands on the newest main. Batch redeploys if several land within a minute. 6) Backfill now: land every finished-but-unlanded build (about 134), oldest first, skipping ones superseded or already on main, with conflict-fix runs where needed. 7) Each land and deploy shows in the Activity Monitor and fix log, with a phone FYI only for failures that need Brett. Tests with fake clashes and a fake failed deploy. Supersedes any auto-land pieces in other builds; don't duplicate.

notes.text: Queued by console.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Reconciled with enforce-the-merge-queue (Nov 10 2026, Brett: 'Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI'). Step 1 must not push to main: a finished build gets its PR and joins the merge queue (push-banner land/merge-queue.mjs enlist does this every 3 min already); the queue batches the ready PRs into one build on queue/batch, runs CI once and lands it on main as one commit. Redeploy-on-land happens once per landed batch. Keep the backfill: it should open PRs into the queue, not push.
Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: You realize when you don't merge stuff right away you have to pull in main again, and tests are gonna fail. Why do you not just merge this as soon as it's done? ... Right, so when something lands, update the console. Period.

steps.text: Design the land pipeline contract inside the orchestrator dispatcher. Define the land-queue state machine (finished → queued → locked → cleaning → merging → testing → pushed → deploying → landed | conflict-fix | deploy-failed). Define a merge lock that lands builds one at a time in finish order. Add a land record schema to the build store (landedAt, mainSha, deployId, attempts, lastError) with a migration that also adds a 'landed' field to existing builds. Write it up in the orchestrator README.
steps.why: Engine internals plus a schema and migration that every later step and the backfill depend on

steps.text: Implement the land core as plain code with no AI. Under the merge lock: delete sync temp files (*.tmp-*) and stray logs (.axf-*.log, .axf-brief.md), clear stale locks, fetch and merge origin/main into the build branch, rerun the build's own tests from its brief/report, then push to main. Return a typed result: landed, clash or tests-failed.
steps.why: Core dispatcher engine path that every land and the backfill run through

steps.text: Wire auto-land into the session-finish handler in the dispatcher. When a build's session ends with all steps ticked and tests green, put it on the land queue straight away, in finish order. Make UI Review non-blocking: screenshots and picks get queued as follow-ups after landing, and changes become follow-up builds. Remove the gates that waited on a person or a later session.

Add conflict-fix runs. On a clash, or on tests failing after the merge, queue a conflict-fix session on the same branch at top priority on any working account, using a fixed prompt template. When it finishes green, put the build back on the land queue. Retry until it is on main, with backoff and an attempts counter in the land record.

Redeploy the console on every land. Pull the auto-update path out of install-console.sh into a callable redeploy script and run it right after each push to main, with no 5-minute timer. Batch redeploys when several lands happen within 60 s. Wait for the health check to pass, then send a refresh event to open consoles.

Rebuild the other apps a land touched. Map the changed paths to apps (AmberX web, axHub web, Molly, …) and rebuild and redeploy each one, with its own health wait. This uses the same batch window as the console redeploy.

Add deploy rollback. Keep a last-good image tag for each app. When a deploy fails or its health check times out, roll back to that tag, record deploy-failed in the land record, and queue a fix build that carries the deploy log.

Report every land and deploy. Emit Activity Monitor events and fix-log entries for queued, landed, conflict-fix, deployed, rolled back and failed. Send a phone FYI only for failures that need Brett: a rollback that also failed, or a build still not on main after N conflict-fix attempts.

Add a Land queue panel to the Activity Monitor UI. It shows the queue, the current lock holder, recent lands and deploys, and conflict-fix runs. It offers these actions: land now, retry, skip, roll back. It has these settings: auto-land on/off and the batch window in seconds.

Give the Land queue full API control, the same across all four surfaces. Deep link: console_show / console_open target 'activity-monitor/land'. State read: the queue, the lock and the land records. Actions: land now, retry, skip, roll back, start backfill. Settings: auto-land and batch window. Expose these through REST routes, MCP console actions and plugin commands, the axf CLI subcommands 'land' and 'deploy', and AmberX voice intents.

Implement the backfill command. List the finished-but-unlanded builds, oldest first. Skip any that are superseded (checked through supersedes links) or already on main (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor or a patch-id match). Put the rest on the land queue, which uses conflict-fix runs where needed. Support a --dry-run report.

Remove the duplicate auto-land pieces. Find the auto-land and merge code in other builds and modules (including build-manager leftovers and the shipping unblock in the orchestrator) and point them at the new land pipeline. Mark the overlapping queued builds as superseded by this one.

Write tests for the land pipeline using temporary git repos. Cover: the merge lock and finish order, a fake code clash leading to a conflict-fix run, a fake test failure after the merge, redeploy batching within 60 s, a fake failed deploy leading to rollback and a fix build, backfill skipping superseded and already-on-main builds, and API parity across REST, MCP and CLI.

Start the backfill. Run it with --dry-run and save the list in the report, then start the real backfill of about 134 builds, oldest first. Watch the first lands and redeploys come up healthy in the Activity Monitor, and note what is still queued.

Final step. Run the full test suite. Write the report at _claude/builds/reports/auto-land-every-build-the-moment-it-finishes-red.md, covering the backfill status and how each feature is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row, then open the PR with the API reach list.

before.title: Projects: create a new project and move builds between projects; move every pending build older than 2 days into a new project
before.detail: 1) Add create-project (valid project manifest, its own builds, notes, data; per the multi-project setup where picking a project switches all data) and move-builds-between-projects, by UI and full API (no AI). 2) Then create a new project and move every Pending build created before 2026-11-08 out of the current project into it, with their notes, steps, branches and history intact; nothing deleted or archived. Builds from the last two days stay. Report the list moved.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Queued by console.
Split by Claude into 10 steps (1 Fable).

origin.said: I don't want to archive. I want to move to another, you know how we set it up from multiple projects. Each one has its own builds, its own notes, all that. Make a new project, remove those from this project and move them to the new project.

steps.text: Design the project contract. Write the project manifest schema covering id, name, created, and the builds, notes and data roots. Define move-build semantics: a build's store entry, journal lines, notes, steps, branches, PR links, reports, shipped records and change entries all move together and keep their ids. Specify the order of operations so a move is atomic (write the target with tmp files, then remove from the source, roll back on failure) and how id collisions are handled. Confirm that a project switch already switches all build data, and write the contract to a doc.
steps.why: Cross-project data contract and schema design that every later step and app depends on

steps.text: Build the createProject core library. Validate the manifest against the schema, scaffold the project's own builds, notes and data folders, register it in the projects registry and the /projects hub sync, and refuse duplicate ids. It is a pure function with no AI. Add unit tests.

Build the moveBuilds core library, following the contract from step 1. Move the selected builds between projects: store entries, journal entries, notes, steps, reports, shipped records and change-entry refs. Git branches and PRs are left untouched, but their references are kept. Writes are atomic with rollback, and a dry-run returns the planned list. Nothing is deleted or archived; the source only loses the moved entries. Add unit tests, including a failure halfway through a move.

Add REST routes for the console API. POST /api/projects creates a project. GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/:id read state. POST /api/projects/:id/move-builds takes {buildIds|filter:{state,createdBefore}, dryRun} and moves builds. GET /api/projects/:id/builds lists a project's builds. Add route tests.

Expose the same actions through the other three channels, all calling the same library functions with the same arguments. MCP: console actions project.create, project.list, project.get and project.moveBuilds. CLI: axf project create|list|show|move-builds with --dry-run, --state and --created-before. Voice: AmberX intents for 'create project X' and 'move builds to project X'.

Add the UI. A New project dialog in the project picker. In the Build manager, multi-select with a 'Move to project…' action that shows a dry-run preview and asks for confirmation. Add the deep links console_show/console_open targets projects/new, projects/<id> and builds/move?ids=…, register them, and make dialog state readable through the API from step 4.

Run end-to-end tests of create and move on a scratch fixture through REST, MCP and CLI. Check that the results match across channels, that history and notes are intact after a move, that switching to the target project shows the moved builds, and that the source no longer lists them.

Do a dry run against the real data. Using the API, list every build in the current project (amberx-axf) whose state is Pending and that was created before 2026-11-08T00:00. Save the list with ids, titles, created dates and branches. Confirm that builds from 2026-11-08 onward are excluded.

Do the real move. Create the new project through the API (id amberx-axf-backlog unless one is already defined, and record the chosen name). Move the dry-run list into it. Verify the counts before and after, check that every moved build's notes, steps, journal and branch refs are present in the target, and confirm nothing was deleted or archived. Commit the data changes.

Finish the build. Run the full test suite. Write the report to _claude/builds/reports/projects-create-a-new-project-and-move-builds-be.md, including the moved-builds list and how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, with the API access paths listed in its description.

before.detail: Amends the Project Manager build. Drag a build (or similar item) from one project and drop it on another project's tab or window. A dialog asks where it goes: Pending, Queued or Planned, showing that project's current queue, pending list and plans. If Queued, pick the position: first, second, third... or last. Full API control.

notes.text: Queued by console.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Drag a build over to another tab or window with the other project and drop it, and a dialog asks if you want to drop into pending, queued or planned. If queued, it asks what spot in the queue, first, second, third or last, while listing the current queue, the current pending, the current plan.

steps.text: Define the cross-tab and cross-window drag-and-drop contract for console items. Add a shared MIME type (application/x-axf-item+json) and payload shape {kind, id, title, sourceProject, sourceList}. Add a drop-target registration API that project tabs and project windows use. Add BroadcastChannel hover and drop-accept feedback between windows of the same console origin. Document the contract.
steps.why: Cross-window drag contract changes how GUIs in every console app exchange items

steps.text: Add the server-side move operation to the Project Manager store. Move a build (or other movable item) from one project to another project's Pending, Queued (with a position: 1-based index or 'last') or Planned list. Validate the item kind and target, clamp the position, write atomically, and record the move in the journal.

Add the REST routes. GET /api/projects/:id/lists returns the current queue (in order), pending and plans for the drop dialog. POST /api/projects/:id/items/move takes {item, from, to: pending|queued|planned, position}. Wire both into the console API router.

Expose the same move and lists operations through every other API surface. Add MCP console actions and plugin commands (project_lists, project_move_item) and control@1 planner-item support for moves into Planned. Add the CLI subcommands 'projects lists <project>' and 'projects move <item> --to <project> --into pending|queued|planned [--position n|first|last]'. Add AmberX voice intents ('move build X to project Y, queue second').

Make build rows (and similar items) in the Project Manager draggable using the new contract. Register each project tab and each project window as a drop target, with hover highlighting and refusal of drops onto the item's own project.

Build the drop dialog. Show the target project's current queue (numbered), pending list and plans. Let the user choose Pending, Queued or Planned. If Queued, show a position picker (first, second, third… last) with a preview of where the item will land. Confirm calls POST /items/move; cancel leaves everything unchanged.

Add full API control for the drop dialog. Add a deep link through console_show / console_open target 'project-manager/move?item=<id>&to=<project>[&into=queued&position=n]' that opens the dialog prefilled. Make the dialog state (open, item, target project, choice, position) readable through REST and MCP. Make its actions (choose list, set position, confirm, cancel) callable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Write the tests. Unit tests for the store move (each target, positions first, middle and last, out-of-range clamp, same-project refusal). Route tests. MCP, CLI and voice parity tests against the same fixture. A UI test of drag, drop, dialog and confirm across two tabs.

Run the full test suite and fix any failures. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/project-manager-add-on-drag-a-build-to-another-p.md. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, stating how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: AmberX Android: web view top banner hidden behind the status bar and camera cutout (respect safe-area insets)
before.detail: In the AmberX Android app the rendered page sits too high: the top banner/row is hidden behind the phone's status bar (call notifications) and the camera cutout. Fix edge-to-edge handling: apply system bar and display-cutout insets (WindowInsets / safe-area-inset-top for the web view), so the top row is fully visible. Test on the paired phone, portrait and landscape.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Fix the top bar of the AmberX app because it's behind my top banner where my call notifications are. It renders the web page too high up for the screen. The top row is hidden. The banner's behind stuff like my camera.

steps.text: Locate the AmberX Android WebView host (activity/fragment, theme, manifest) and the web shell's top-banner CSS; note current edge-to-edge setup (enableEdgeToEdge / setDecorFitsSystemWindows, windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode, viewport meta) and record findings in the build notes.

Native fix: in the WebView host, apply ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener combining WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars() | displayCutout(); pad the WebView container top/left/right/bottom by those insets (portrait and landscape), set layoutInDisplayCutoutMode to shortEdges, and keep status bar icons readable over the banner colour.

Web side: add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta and make the top banner/row use padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top) (plus left/right for landscape cutouts), with a JS bridge fallback that sets --sat/--sal/--sar/--sab CSS variables from the native insets for WebView versions where env() reports 0; ensure no double padding with the native fix.

API part: expose the applied insets and edge-to-edge mode as readable state (top/left/right/bottom px, cutout present, orientation) via the console API REST route, an MCP console action, the CLI (`axf amberx insets`) and an AmberX voice query, all returning the same payload; reuse the existing console_show/console_open deep link for the AmberX app view. No new settings or actions are added (layout fix only).

Tests: add an instrumented/Robolectric test that dispatches fake WindowInsets (status bar 32dp + top cutout, then landscape side cutout) and asserts the WebView container padding; add a web unit test for the safe-area CSS variables; add an API test for the insets state read across REST/MCP/CLI.

Build the debug APK, install on the paired phone via adb, verify portrait and landscape (with an active call notification) that the top row is fully visible and not under the status bar or camera cutout; capture adb screenshots plus the insets state read output as evidence.

Run the full test suites, write the report (_claude/builds/reports/amberx-android-web-view-top-banner-hidden-behind.md) with before/after screenshots and how the insets state is reached via deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating the same API reach.

before.title: Plugin UI inventory + per-plugin reskin: one button lists every element, behavior and token; rebuild just that plugin's look
before.detail: New plugin. 1) A button in every plugin's settings: generates a full inventory of that plugin's UI: every dialog, table, button, pane, window, tab and other element, every behavior, and every layout, style and colour token. 2) Views: grid with expandable rows, classic tree, 3D, IDE-style tab groups; selectable roots; groups of elements. 3) Reskin / rebuild just that plugin: regenerate its look, layout and behavior as a skin scoped to the one plugin (same code underneath, not rewritten from scratch), to look better, perform better, or be new. Preview before apply, one-click revert. Full API/CLI control; AI only behind its switch.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 15 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: A button in every plugin's settings. Generates a list of all the UI's dialogs, tables, buttons, panes, windows, tabs, everything, every behavior, every layout, style and color token. Multiple views, 3D, grid, expandable rows, classical trees, different roots, IDE style tabs. Rebuild, it will reskin just that plugin instead of the whole room. New look, layout and behavior, to look better, perform better, or be new.

steps.text: Design the inventory contract: a versioned JSON schema for one plugin's UI inventory (elements with kind dialog/table/button/pane/window/tab/other, parent/child ids, behaviors as event→action entries, layout/style/colour tokens with source and resolved value, groups and roots), plus the skin contract (a per-plugin skin manifest of token overrides, layout overrides and behavior toggles, keyed by plugin id and versioned so revert is exact). Write the schema files and a short contract doc.
steps.why: Cross-port contract every plugin's UI must satisfy, used by inventory, views and skins

steps.text: Framework skin scoping: add a plugin-scoped skin layer to the framework so a skin applies only inside one plugin's mount root (scoped CSS custom properties and layout overrides under the plugin's container, behavior toggles through the existing component props), with load order room theme → plugin skin and a no-op when no skin is set. Same component code underneath.
steps.why: Changes how GUIs render across all apps: a new framework layer between room theme and plugin

steps.text: Framework inventory hooks: expose a read-only introspection walk over a mounted plugin (component tree, registered dialogs/windows/tabs, bound event handlers, resolved tokens) that returns data matching the inventory schema, without changing plugin code.
steps.why: Kernel/engine internals: framework-level introspection of every plugin's component tree

steps.text: Scaffold the new ui-inventory plugin: manifest, server entry, store for inventories and skins (per plugin, with history for revert), settings (AI switch off by default), and register it with the plugin installer.

Inventory generator: build the full inventory for one plugin from the framework walk plus a static pass over the plugin's source and styles (catches dialogs and tabs not currently mounted), merge, validate against the schema and save with a timestamp.

Add the 'UI inventory' button to every plugin's settings through the shared settings frame (one injection point, not per-plugin edits); clicking it generates the inventory and opens the viewer on that plugin. API part in the same step: REST POST /api/ui-inventory/:plugin/generate and GET /api/ui-inventory/:plugin, MCP console actions ui_inventory.generate / ui_inventory.get, CLI `axf ui-inventory generate|show <plugin>`, voice intent 'list the UI of <plugin>', deep link console_open target ui-inventory?plugin=<id>.

Viewer shell with IDE-style tab groups (split, drag tabs between groups, each tab is one view on one root) and the root/group picker: choose any element as root, define and save named groups of elements.
Grid view with expandable rows (element, kind, behaviors, tokens; filter, sort, search) and classic tree view, both rooted at the selected root or group.
3D view: elements as nested layered boxes by containment depth, orbit/zoom, click to select and sync selection with the other views; falls back to tree when WebGL is missing.

API for the viewer: deep links for plugin, view, root, group and tab layout; state read (open tabs, views, root, selection, groups); actions open_view, set_root, select, create/rename/delete group, move tab, export inventory (JSON/CSV). REST + MCP + CLI + voice, all four the same.

Reskin generator without AI: from the inventory, produce a skin for the one plugin by goal (look better: spacing/contrast/type scale fixes; perform better: drop heavy effects, virtualise long tables, lazy tabs; new: preset palettes and layouts), editable token/layout/behavior overrides, validated against the skin schema.

AI reskin behind the plugin's AI switch: when on, send the inventory and goal to the configured model to propose a skin; output goes through the same validator; when off, the option is hidden and the API returns a clear 'AI is off' error.
Reskin UI: 'Rebuild this plugin' panel with goal picker, override editor, side-by-side live preview (skin applied only inside a preview mount of the plugin), Apply, one-click Revert and skin history.

API for reskin: deep link to the reskin panel for a plugin; state read (active skin, preview skin, history); actions generate, preview, apply, revert, revert_to <version>, set override, AI switch setting. REST + MCP + CLI + voice, all four the same.

Tests, report, THREADS row and PR: unit tests for schema validation, introspection walk, static scan, skin scoping (no leak outside the plugin root), apply/revert round trip and API parity across REST/MCP/CLI/voice; write _claude/builds/reports/plugin-ui-inventory-per-plugin-reskin-one-button.md; add the THREADS row; open the PR stating how each UI is reached (deep link, state, actions, settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

before.title: Shared screenshot registry hooked everywhere + live edit from a screenshot + new per-screen skin asset type
before.detail: 1) Shared screenshot registry reachable from anywhere by hook (not only UI Review): Shipped Features entries, Plan Studio plans, orchestrator builds (Build Manager is being retired), errors, any mention of a build/feature/error links its screenshots. 2) Opening a screenshot of an element: side pane with every token/style/parameter for that screen; tweak live with a hot-rendered live preview of the same screen; Save. 3) New asset type: screen skin (colour, style, layout, behavior, icon themes etc.) applied to one particular UI screen only. Full API/CLI control.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 14 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: Screenshots go into a shared registry that can be accessed from anywhere. Plan Studio, features, builds, errors tie into it through a hook, not directly through UI review. View the screenshot of an element, open a pane with all the tokens, styles, parameters, tweak it live with a hot rendering preview of the same screen, save it. That creates a new asset type with the color, style, layout, behavior, icon themes that applies to just a particular UI screen.

steps.text: Design the shared screenshot registry: record schema (id, screen id, element selector, app, captured_at, file path, links[] of {kind: build|feature|plan|error, ref}), storage layout, and a migration that imports existing UI Review screenshots into it without losing their current links.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for a store shared across apps

steps.text: Define the screenshot hook contract (screenshots.attach / screenshots.forRef / screenshots.onCapture) that any plugin calls to link or list screenshots by ref, with a typed event payload. UI Review becomes one caller of the hook, not its owner.
steps.why: Cross-port contract every app and plugin builds against

steps.text: Design the screen skin asset type: schema (target screen id, colour tokens, style overrides, layout params, behavior flags, icon theme), versioning, and the migration that registers it beside the existing asset types.
steps.why: New asset schema and migration in the shared asset store

steps.text: Theming engine: resolve the token stack as global theme → app theme → screen skin for the active screen id only, plus a hot-apply path that pushes a draft skin into a render without saving it.
steps.why: Engine internals that change how GUIs are themed across apps

steps.text: Implement the screenshot registry store and REST routes (list, get, by ref, attach, detach, delete), using the step 1 schema, and run the UI Review migration.
Hook callers: Shipped Features entries, Plan Studio plans, orchestrator builds, and the errors log call screenshots.attach and forRef. Remove any Build Manager-only paths.
Mention linker: anywhere a build, feature or error id is rendered (shared ref chip component), show a screenshot count and thumbnail strip from the registry.

Registry API parity: console_show/console_open target 'screenshots' and 'screenshot/<id>' deep links, state read, MCP tools (screenshots_list/get/attach/detach), CLI 'axf screenshots …', and AmberX voice intents.
Screen skin asset store and REST routes (create, get, list by screen, update, delete, apply, unapply) on top of the step 3 schema.

Screenshot viewer side pane: when you open a screenshot of an element, list every token, style and parameter for that screen, grouped as colour, style, layout, behavior and icons, with editable fields.
Live preview: render the same screen in an iframe or sandbox, hot-apply pane edits through theme hot-apply, then Save to create or update the screen skin asset, with Revert and Discard.

Skin editor and screen skin API parity: deep links (console_open 'screenshot/<id>/edit', 'asset/screen-skin/<id>'), state read of the draft and saved skin, actions and settings (set token, preview, save, revert, apply, unapply) via REST, MCP console actions and plugin commands, CLI 'axf skins …', and voice.
Docs: registry hook usage for plugin authors, screen skin asset type, and the API reach table (deep link, state, actions, settings across REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

Tests (registry store, migration, hook callers, skin resolve order, hot-apply, REST/MCP/CLI parity), report at _claude/builds/reports/shared-screenshot-registry-hooked-everywhere-liv.md, THREADS row, and PR stating how each UI is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Shipped Features: show each landed build's screenshots on its entry
before.detail: Each Shipped Features entry shows the screenshots and before/after shots of what that build did (pulled from the shared screenshot registry / UI Review screenshots grouped by build name), inline with a gallery view. Goes with the shared screenshot registry build.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 7 steps (1 Fable).

origin.said: Screenshots and everything of what it did? Yep.

steps.text: Define the contract between Shipped Features entries and the shared screenshot registry: how a build id/name maps to its screenshots, how before/after pairs are marked (role: before|after|shot, pair key, caption, captured_at, source = registry|ui-review), and the fallback lookup through UI Review screenshots grouped by build name. Write it as a schema doc and a JSON schema both sides read; if the shared screenshot registry build has not landed, define the read interface it must satisfy.
steps.why: Cross-port contract between the screenshot registry, UI Review and Shipped Features

steps.text: Server side: add a resolver that, for a shipped build, collects its screenshots from the shared screenshot registry (and UI Review screenshots grouped by build name as fallback), pairs before/after shots, dedupes, and returns them sorted and capped per the contract. Cache per build id.

REST API: GET /api/shipped/:id/screenshots (list, pairs, counts) and GET /api/shipped/:id/screenshots/:shot (one shot with metadata and image URL); include screenshot count and cover thumbnail on the existing shipped list/entry responses. Settings for the gallery (default view grid|before-after, thumbnail size, show on list on/off) readable and writable at GET/PUT /api/shipped/settings/gallery.

UI: on each Shipped Features entry show an inline screenshot strip (cover + count) and a gallery view: grid of shots, before/after side-by-side or slider for pairs, lightbox with prev/next and captions, empty state when the build has none. Built on the console plugin framework components.

API parity for the gallery UI: deep links console_show/console_open targets shipped-features/<build id>/screenshots and shipped-features/<build id>/screenshots/<shot> (opens gallery or lightbox at that shot, before/after mode); gallery state readable (open build, current shot, view mode); actions open_gallery, show_shot, next/prev, set_view, and gallery settings registered as console actions for MCP.

CLI and voice: add 'shipped screenshots <build> [--shot n] [--before-after] [--open]' and 'shipped gallery settings get|set' plugin commands calling the same REST/actions; add AmberX voice intents ('show me the screenshots for <build>', 'next shot', 'before and after') mapped to the same actions.

Tests: resolver (registry hit, UI Review fallback, before/after pairing, no screenshots), REST endpoints and settings, deep link parsing, action/MCP/CLI/voice parity (same results through all four), and a UI test that the gallery renders and the lightbox navigates. Then write the report _claude/builds/reports/shipped-features-show-each-landed-build-s-screen.md (what changed, screenshots of the gallery, how each UI part is reached via deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice), add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating the API reach for every UI piece and the dependency on the shared screenshot registry build.

before.detail: Amends per-plugin appearance saves and skins-as-packages. 1) A save captures the plugin's full state: behavior, style, layout, colour, icons and any code-level overrides, not just the changed category. 2) A skin is only a manifest of asset names per section. 3) Skins must apply consistently to every plugin screen even though plugins use different asset names than the host app: add a shared asset naming contract + alias map (plugin asset -> canonical role, e.g. toolbar, panel, primary button) so one skin resolves the same look across apps and plugins. before.title: Skin rule: overrides are local only; global changes only by applying a whole skin
before.detail: Amends the skins naming-contract build. Precedence: axHub base < skin (by canonical role) < per-screen skin < per-element override. An override changes only that element. Global changes are made ONLY by applying a whole skin; editing a button inside one plugin or app never propagates to other plugins/apps. Enforce in the inline editor (no 'apply everywhere' outside the skin editor) and document in CLAUDE.md rules.

If *.amberxai.com wildcard DNS already points at the VPS, no Hostinger change is needed; if not, record the exact A record needed (Hostinger API key is missing from the axHub vault, so report it). Any change in the asset's own settings becomes an override of the app's global settings for that asset. In the app's main Settings, every option overridden by an asset is greyed out with the note 'Controlled by <asset name>' and a link that opens that asset's settings interface. Pairs with the bug fix that makes asset settings target the right-clicked asset.

before.title: Molly gap: axHub allows Molly's origin on /auth/api/* (CORS with credentials) so native screens read the hub session
before.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. From https://molly.amberxai.com, GET https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/api/session answers 200 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and the preflight OPTIONS /auth/api/logout answers 200 with no CORS headers, so a browser on Molly cannot read the hub session or post a write. The hub should answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins (Molly first) on /auth/api/* with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true, Access-Control-Allow-Headers content-type, accept, x-axhub-csrf, Vary Origin; never * with credentials. The session cookie is same-site (SameSite=Lax is enough). Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (axhub provider, credentials include, X-AxHub-CSRF on writes).

before.title: Molly gap: the console frame hands Molly its token once (embed@1 credentials) and the console API allows Molly's origin
before.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. Two halves. (1) The console API refuses cross-origin calls from Molly: OPTIONS https://console.amberxai.com/api/me with Origin https://molly.amberxai.com answers 401 with no CORS headers (the token check runs before FastAPI's CORSMiddleware, and allow_origins * cannot be used by the wall). Let preflights through and answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins with Access-Control-Allow-Headers authorization, content-type, accept. (2) The console token lives only in the console origin's storage (axf-console:token); Molly keeps its own copy (molly:console-token) that today a person must paste. Add an embed@1 message (guest to host, e.g. credentials with {app, scheme, token}) the console frame sends once to a host it recognises (frame-ancestors origin, embed host name), handled by Molly's xLayout host into the console provider's signIn(token); never to a URL or a log. Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (console provider, bearer, credentials omit).

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-11T00:06:50.193Z
> I gotta make sure nothing that's built or that I've written gets overwritten or broken from one of those old branches. Go one by one and I'll tell you to merge it or not.

## What to build
Continue build "Merge review, one by one: every built-but-unmerged build checked against current main, Brett decides merge or not" (merge-review-one-by-one-every-built-but-unmerged) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-11 00:06):
"I gotta make sure nothing that's built or that I've written gets overwritten or broken from one of those old branches. Go one by one and I'll tell you to merge it or not."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

before.title: Skins are a complete rework: look + layout + behavior, and professional skins
before.detail: After skins-finish lands (skin@1 + skin-coverage@1 for every asset type). Today a skin covers look only; layout and behavior live in design packs. Change: a skin is the complete rework of an app. Extend skin@1 (contract, Fable) to carry everything a design pack does: look (colors, grid and hover/selection colors, typography sizes, spacing/density, radius, borders, shadows, icons, motion), layout (nav placement, app menu, toolbars, banners, panel arrangement, grid density) and behavior (how menus open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions, overflow rules) for every registry asset type: nav menu, app menu, context menu, grids, dialogs, windows, bars, widgets, text. Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. Then design at least 5 complete professional skins (clean enterprise, dark pro, compact data, modern SaaS, plus one more), applied to the real console, AmberX and Molly; post each to UI Review with desktop and phone shots; the pick becomes the default. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests; report.

steps.text: Extend the skin@1 contract so one skin carries everything a design pack does. steps.text: Design the schema and migration that fold design packs into skins. Map each design-pack field to a skin@1 field, write a versioned migration for stored packs and user selections, and add a design-pack compatibility alias that resolves to the skin, with a deprecation note.
steps.why: Schema plus migration design across stored data and contracts

steps.why: Changes how layout works across all apps

steps.text: Make the framework behavior runtime skin-driven. Menu open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions and overflow rules should all come from the active skin, for every asset type in the registry.
steps.why: Changes how GUI behavior works across all apps

Surfaces: REST routes on the console API, MCP tools as console actions and plugin commands, CLI subcommands, and AmberX voice intents. Add console_show / console_open targets.

Design the professional skin 'Dark Pro' with complete look, layout and behavior for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'Compact Data': dense grids, tight spacing, data-first layout, with complete coverage for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'Modern SaaS' with complete look, layout and behavior for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'High Contrast Accessible' (WCAG AAA contrast, larger targets, reduced motion), with complete coverage for every asset type.

Capture desktop and phone screenshots of each skin on the console, AmberX and Molly, then post each skin to UI Review. Wire it so the picked skin becomes the default. API part: make the default readable and settable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.
Update the docs: skin@1 authoring guide (look, layout, behavior), design-pack migration and alias, and how to reach each skin feature through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T16:42:29.017Z
> We need to remove all the styling and theme and layout stuff. Remove it all because the new thing's going to override it.

## What to build
Continue build "Remove the old theme manager, style and layout settings everywhere; skins replace them" (remove-the-old-theme-manager-style-and-layout-se) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 16:42):
"We need to remove all the styling and theme and layout stuff. Remove it all because the new thing's going to override it."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

Write the schema and the migration module.
[ ] s3 (~30 min) Change the shared GUI framework: remove the theme manager, style-theme loader and layout-setting hooks from the app shell, so skins (with their colour theme) are the only thing that applies look and layout. Route any remaining readers of the old keys through the active skin, and call the migration from step 2 on startup.
